articles.title: Jamie Carragher: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta becoming like Sir Alex Ferguson after ref criticism of Sunderland penalty
articles.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta described the penalty given against them in their 2-0 win over Sunderland as “unacceptable”; Gunners have sought an explanation from Pro Ref over penalty award; Jamie Carragher said: "This was Mikel Arteta becoming the Alex Ferguson of the PL now"
articles.body:
A furious Arteta described the saved second-half penalty as "unacceptable" after referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa brought down Dan Ballard.

The Gunners have subsequently sought an explanation from refereeing body Pro Ref over the penalty award.

Arteta's anger has led Carragher to draw a comparison with ex-Manchester United boss Ferguson, who was famously unafraid to publicly criticise match officials, even while his side were the dominant domestic force.

Arsenal did not concede a penalty in last season's title-winning campaign and Carragher believes "don" Arteta is using his Premier League-champion status to influence referees' decision-making.

He told Monday Night Football : "This was Mikel Arteta becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now.

"He's the don at the moment; he's the Premier League champion.

"A lot of new managers about... he's been in his role for six or seven years, and he feels he's in a position of power to say, 'Yeah, it wasn't a penalty'. And I don't think it was a penalty.

"But it'd be interesting to see how long it takes for another referee to give a penalty against Arsenal in a similar situation.

"I thought it was very interesting in the press conference; one of the journalists made a point about, no matter what question you asked him, he kept going back to the penalty, so he was determined to get the narrative out that this won't happen again to his club.

"But that's a manager - we've seen it with Sir Alex Ferguson, we've seen it with Jose Mourinho."

Former Luton, Middlesbrough and Wolves boss Rob Edwards was the special guest on MNF and concurred with Carragher's view on Arteta.

He said: "I think Jamie's right. He's put himself into a position now where he's looking after his team and his football club, and people will listen to the Premier League-winning manager, won't they?

"They will listen to him; he's a powerful voice there now."

Arsenal are set to hold talks with Pro Ref over the penalty Sunderland were awarded on Saturday.

The Gunners want an explanation for why the penalty was given on the field and then approved by VAR.

Arsenal have regularly asked Pro Ref for consistency in refereeing decisions.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said at his post-match press conference at the Stadium of Light:

"The first question we have to discuss is this. This is not acceptable at this level.

"It was a beautiful game of football with two teams, with an atmosphere in the stadium that was unbelievable.

"Sunderland are so well organised, they are so good in so many phases, they have great players and they create a lot of issues. We have to cope with all of that in a really difficult week.

"And on top of that, we have to go through what we have done today, that, in my opinion, is not acceptable.

"I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation, or the way the VAR has to intervene.

"I'm sad that we have to discuss this after such a beautiful game, that at this level, has the gravity of that. Because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.

"At this level, with all the work we put in, this cannot happen."

articles.title: Ousmane Dembélé gives humble Ballon d’Or response, unlike Kylian Mbappé, who says he is ‘the chosen one’
articles.summary: Football News: Ousmane Dembélé shares his thoughts on the Ballon d'Or and offers a humble perspective, contrasting with Kylian Mbappé's bold claims of being 'the chosen one'. Dembélé emphasizes hard work over expectations as he enters the award race as the reigning champion.
articles.body: Ousmane Dembélé has taken a subtle dig at Kylian Mbappé’s recent remarks, offering a far more humble view of his rise to the top. While Mbappé has made no secret of believing he deserves the Ballon d’Or, Dembélé has stressed that he never saw himself as the obvious star destined to reach the summit, instead putting his success down to years of hard work.Ousmane Dembélé says he was never 'the chosen one'Dembélé was speaking after PSG’s 1-0 victory over Brest when he was asked about his chances of winning the Ballon d’Or for a second consecutive year.The 29-year-old appeared to reference comments recently made by Mbappé, who described the different expectations surrounding the pair during their careers.“Dembélé? He was always seen as a talented player. I, on the other hand, was always seen as the chosen one,” Mbappé told France Football.Dembélé offered his own description of the path that took him to the top.“I've always been at the back of the class working hard,” he said.“Throughout my career, I haven't said a word, I've worked incredibly hard.“Like I said, I was never the chosen one, but I worked hard and last year I was rewarded after a fantastic year with Paris Saint-Germain.“And this year, we'll see how it goes -- no pressure, taking it easy.”It was a striking contrast to the image Mbappé described, with Dembélé portraying himself as a player who had to keep working while others were more readily identified as future superstars.Dembélé believes another PSG player could win the Ballon d'OrDembélé enters the new Ballon d’Or race as the reigning holder of the award after the most successful season of his career.He became the sixth Frenchman to win the Ballon d’Or last year, having played a starring role in PSG’s historic campaign under Luis Enrique.Dembélé scored 35 goals in all competitions as PSG won Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and the club’s first Champions League title.That European triumph was particularly emphatic, with PSG beating Inter Milan 5-0 in the final.Yet Dembélé does not appear convinced that his own success makes him the inevitable favourite this time around.Last week, he named Harry Kane, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Mbappé as his three leading candidates for the prize.But he also suggested the award could remain in Paris.“I don't think this trophy is unpredictable. I think it will remain in the hands of a Paris Saint-Germain player,” he said.Mbappé, meanwhile, left PSG for Real Madrid in 2024 and finished seventh in the 2025 Ballon d’Or voting despite scoring 44 goals in his debut season in Spain.The Real Madrid forward has since made a forceful case for the 2026 award, despite ending the season without major silverware. Mbappé scored 42 goals in 44 club appearances, won the World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals and took his career World Cup tally to a record 22 goals. He has also insisted that the Ballon d’Or is an individual award rather than simply a reward for team success, declaring: “There was no player better than me.”The pair therefore enter the latest race from very different positions: Dembélé as the defending champion and Mbappé as the former PSG superstar now trying to claim the prize with Real Madrid.Dembélé is building PSG's attack without MbappéWhile the Ballon d’Or conversation places Dembélé and Mbappé against each other, Dembélé's immediate focus is on maintaining PSG's attacking standards without his former team-mate.The French forward has developed a productive understanding with Spanish striker Ferran Torres, who has become an important part of the reshaped PSG attack.Dembélé already knew Torres from their time together at Barcelona and believes that familiarity has helped them quickly establish a connection.“I was lucky enough to play with him a bit at Barcelona,” Dembélé said.“He's a true goalscorer, a true number nine who can also play on the wing. And it's easy to play with him. He makes very good runs. It's easy to find him, we talk a lot, it's easy with Ferran.”The partnership gives Dembélé another route to influence games as PSG continue life after Mbappé, while the Ballon d’Or debate provides an increasingly intriguing backdrop to the two French stars' contrasting careers.For Dembélé, though, the central theme remains the same one he has returned to throughout his career: he may not have been the player everyone expected to reach the summit, but he worked until he got there.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 48-year-old father of 3 makes college football debut
articles.summary: Justin Buzzard says he feels both "good" and "sore all the time."
articles.body:
A California father of three is proving age might be just a number after all, making his college football debut at 48 years old.

Justin Buzzard, who also happens to wear a No. 48 jersey, is a freshman defensive end for the San Jose City College Jaguars.

"I feel good," Buzzard told ABC News' Danny New after his first game. "I mean, I'm sore all the time."

"I haven't hit anyone in a football game in 30 years, so that felt good to do," he added.

Buzzard previously registered to play football for Whitworth University in Washington 30 years ago, but was redshirted and sustained an injury before he could start playing.

Decades later, Buzzard's son encouraged him to return to the field when he heard stories of other older men playing college sports in their later years.

"I came up with the pro-con list. The pro list was super long. The con list was, 'What if I got hurt?'" Buzzard recalled of his decision-making process.

San Jose City College was also open to giving Buzzard a chance, so he said he immediately went to work, weightlifting and putting on 10 pounds of muscle.

"I'm just sprinting all the time, so my hamstrings are on fire," Buzzard said now of his exercise routine.

Today, Buzzard said he and two of his sons, who play high school football, like to trade tips and techniques with each other.

Buzzard is also already making an impact three weeks into the season and recorded a pass breakup over the weekend.

Even though practice sessions have been harder than he initially anticipated, Buzzard said he has realized he can achieve what he puts his mind to.

"At the same time … I just realized I can do this," he said.

articles.title: Texas QB Arch Manning thought a fake AI video of Steve Sarkisian hitting a woman after their win over Ohio State was hilarious
articles.summary: The moment, days after a high for the Longhorns program, was not a good one for Arch Manning.
articles.body:
Arch Manning thought an AI edit of his football coach hitting a longtime ESPN reporter after their wild comeback win over Ohio State on Saturday night was hilarious.

The Texas quarterback was asked on Monday if he saw any edits on social media after the Longhorns rallied to knock off No. 1 Ohio State 24-23 on Saturday night in Austin. Quickly, he remembered a fake video that showed Texas coach Steve Sarkisian slapping longtime ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe.

Manning thought the fake video, which depicted a man hitting a woman, was incredibly funny.

"I saw an AI edit of Sark's interview. Have y'all seen that one?" Manning said, laughing. "That's a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe? It's hilarious."

The fake video came after an awkward moment between Rowe, who has been an ESPN staple for decades, and Sarkisian after the game on Saturday night. Sarkisian essentially blew her off while she was trying to talk to him on live TV.

"That's called Texas fight! That's called Texas fight! Hook 'em!" Sarkisian yelled into the mic before just walking away from Rowe, completely ignoring her question. Rowe looked, understandably, frustrated.

ESPN's Laura Rutledge also tried to talk to Sarkisian at halftime at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, but that interview was derailed due to technical difficulties.

Manning went 23 of 37 for 195 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the win, which vaulted the Longhorns to No. 1 in the country. They rallied from a 23-3 deficit in the second half, absolutely stunning the Buckeyes.

While Manning pulled off the comeback win, one of the best in recent Longhorns memory, his comments on Monday about a fake video of his football coach hitting a woman reporter for trying to do her job were undoubtedly poor. It's a rough look in the wake of a high for the program.

But based on the reaction in the room when Manning was laughing about it, it doesn't seem likely that anything will come of it.

articles.title: Memorial Linebacker commits to Dayton Flyers
articles.summary: EVANSVILLE, In. (WEHT) — One of the most talented players in the Tri-State is announcing his commitment to play college football at the Division One level. T...
articles.body:
EVANSVILLE, In. (WEHT) -- One of the most talented players in the Tri-State is announcing his commitment to play college football at the Division One level. Tigers' Grayson Carter will play for Dayton next year turning in his Tiger stripes to become a Flyer. The senior linebacker leads the team with 42 tackles in just four weeks of play. Three of those have been for a loss, and he's been a focal point for a Memorial defense that's only allowing 15 points per game. Carter says he had several other schools to choose from like S.I.U.E., Yale, and Brown. But Dayton's coaching staff stood out among the rest.

"Dayton was probably the biggest school recruiting me like the most. The coach just really made it seem like they really, really wanted me. And then getting on campus, I saw the campus was really, really nice. I really like the school, so it just seemed like the best fit for me." said Carter, "I went on a gameday visit after they offered me and watching the team, like everything just felt really, really good. I just don't have any doubts about it. So I was like, why am I waiting?"

Carter says he's thankful his recruiting decision is already made now he can focus fully on the season trying to help lead the Tigers to their first state title since 2019.

articles.body:
Liverpool host Tottenham Hotspur in the Carabao Cup third round on Tuesday, with Andy Robertson returning to Anfield for the first time since leaving the club this summer, this time as a Spurs player.

Andoni Iraola 's side are unbeaten in five matches under their new head coach, while Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham arrive under mounting pressure after four Premier League games without a win or a goal. Liverpool are the competition's most successful club with 10 titles and have lost only two of their last 20 meetings with Tottenham, who have not won at Anfield in any competition in 15 years.

De Zerbi, though, has said he wants a strong run in the cup competitions this season, and Robertson, who spent nine years on Merseyside before his free transfer in the summer, is expected to start against his former club.

Liverpool vs Tottenham Hotspur – Match preview and team news

Date: Tuesday, 15 September 2026 Kick-off: 20:00 BST Venue: Anfield Referee: Andy Madley Last meeting: Liverpool 1-1 Tottenham Hotspur (Premier League, 15 March 2026)

Conor Bradley , Federico Chiesa , Hugo Ekitike and Giovanni Leoni remain sidelined for Liverpool, though Joe Gomez is back in training and available for selection. Iraola has confirmed Giorgi Mamardashvili will start in goal in place of Alisson , with widespread changes expected elsewhere after a lacklustre performance in Saturday's goalless draw with Fulham .

Tottenham will be without Sandro Tonali (knock), Pedro Porro (muscle) and Dejan Kulusevski , while Richarlison remains frozen out of De Zerbi's plans despite being eligible for cup selection. Destiny Udogie returns to contention after missing the draw with Everton , and De Zerbi has indicated he will not make wholesale changes given the pressure already on his side.

Liverpool remain unbeaten under Iraola but have won only once in five matches, most recently held goalless at home by Fulham despite an encouraging Champions League win over Atletico Madrid in midweek. The head coach has been candid about a lack of control in midfield, with question marks growing over how his side manage games without their front players pressing effectively.

Tottenham's start under De Zerbi has been alarming, with the club yet to score in four Premier League matches following a summer outlay of close to £350million. Back-to-back goalless draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton have left Spurs 17th in the table, and De Zerbi has openly discussed the physical toll of a disrupted pre-season on several key players.

articles.title: Ipswich Town vs Arsenal – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Arsenal begin their Carabao Cup campaign away to Ipswich Town on Tuesday, with the reigning Premier League champions still chasing a first triumph in the com...
articles.body:
Arsenal begin their Carabao Cup campaign away to Ipswich Town on Tuesday, with the reigning Premier League champions still chasing a first triumph in the competition since 1993. Mikel Arteta's side head to Portman Road on the back of six straight wins in all competitions, while Gary O'Neil's Ipswich, back in the top flight after promotion, arrive full of confidence having also collected back-to-back victories over Crystal Palace and Leicester City.

Arsenal have not lifted this trophy since Paul Merson and Steve Morrow inspired victory over Sheffield Wednesday in 1993, and have lost four finals since, most recently to Manchester City last season. Their only previous meeting with Ipswich in the competition came in the 2010-11 semi-finals, when the Tractor Boys won the first leg 1-0 before a 3-0 reverse at the Emirates ended their run. Ipswich striker Chuba Akpom , a product of Arsenal's academy, could face his boyhood club for the first time.

Ipswich Town vs Arsenal – Match preview and team news

Last meeting: Arsenal 4-0 Ipswich Town (Premier League, April 2025)

Ipswich's only fresh absentees are Jack Taylor (knee) and Azor Matusiwa (thigh), neither of whom has featured this season. Emersonn came off with quad tightness against Crystal Palace, but O'Neil said the striker would likely have been rested regardless, with Zian Flemming – eligible for Ipswich despite appearing for Burnley earlier in the competition – his likely replacement.

Arsenal will again be without William Saliba (back), who is not due back for a couple of months, while Ben White is a fresh concern after limping off with a groin issue against Sunderland . Cristhian Mosquera remains a doubt of his own, and Arteta is expected to make close to nine changes, with Kepa Arrizabalaga set to continue as his cup goalkeeper and Viktor Gyokeres in line to lead the line.

Ipswich have settled quickly back into Premier League life, following an opening win over Sunderland with victories over Leicester in the cup and a dramatic comeback against Crystal Palace, sealed by Zian Flemming's 90th-minute winner after Axel Disasi 's first-half red card. The defensive numbers remain a concern, though, with O'Neil's side yet to keep a clean sheet and having shipped nine goals across their last three matches.

Arsenal's perfect start to the season continued at Sunderland on Saturday, where Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka 's second-half goals secured a 2-0 win despite a contentious penalty award that David Raya saved. Victory would extend Arsenal's winning start to the campaign, Community Shield included, to seven games for the first time since 2004-05, with the Gunners having kept five clean sheets from six matches so far.

articles.title: David Sánchez: "No imagino a Messi decir o pedir o mendigar un Balón de Oro"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco cuestiona el protagonismo de Mbappé y Lamine Yamal en la carrera por el galardón
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco cuestiona el protagonismo de Mbappé y Lamine Yamal en la carrera por el galardón
articles.body: La carrera por el próximo Balón de Oro ya ha comenzado a generar debate y David Sánchez no se ha mordido la lengua en La Tribu. El presentador de Despierta San Francisco considera que la pugna entre Kylian Mbappé y Lamine Yamal puede hacerse "muy pesada" y critica el protagonismo que ambos han adquirido en torno al galardón. "Se va a hacer muy pesada la carrera por ganar el Balón de Oro esta temporada", afirmó David Sánchez, que fue especialmente contundente al referirse a los dos jugadores: "Tanto Mbappé como Lamine ya son cansinos en la primera semana de esa carrera hacia dicho galardón". En el caso de Mbappé, el colaborador puso el foco en los títulos conquistados esta temporada: "No ha ganado ni un solo título esta temporada, ha ganado los mismos que yo". Sobre Lamine Yamal, su crítica fue diferente y estuvo relacionada con la consideración del propio jugador sobre sus opciones: "Está muy feo decirse que uno es el mejor del mundo, sea la disciplina que practique cada uno". David Sánchez también dejó claro qué perfil de ganador preferiría. "Ojalá lo gane Rodri, ojalá lo gane Kane, ojalá lo gane cualquiera que no se autoseñale como el máximo candidato para ganar ese Balón de Oro", señaló. David Sánchez recurrió a Lionel Messi para explicar su postura. "De verdad que no imagino a Messi decir o pedir o mendigar un Balón de Oro y dar los argumentos que le posicionen como el favorito para ganar", afirmó. David Sánchez reconoció, eso sí, el nivel de los dos futbolistas señalados como protagonistas de la carrera. "Lamine es espectacular, Mbappé es un pedazo delantero", admitió antes de volver a defender que el premio recaiga en un jugador que no haya reclamado públicamente ese reconocimiento. "Si lo gana Kane, que no lo ha pedido, mejor que mejor. Y si es Rodri, ni os cuento", concluyó.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca: How Man City manager is tackling the toughest job in football
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca seemingly took on an impossible job in the summer when replacing the legendary Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, but is making it look an easy task in the early stages of his tenure.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca seemingly took on an impossible job in the summer when replacing the legendary Pep Guardiola at Manchester City , but is making it look an easy task in the infancy of his tenure.

Four victories in as many games has City sitting joint-top of the Premier League alongside Arsenal , and the early signs suggest those two sides will be the ones tussling for the title once more.

Maresca clinched his most significant win since taking charge with an impressive 1-0 victory against rivals Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, despite playing much of the game with 10 men following Phil Foden's sending-off.

The City players, though, mirrored their manager's feelings by staying calm, and it is this type of composure which has been the most impressive aspect during these first few weeks.

Cool with the media & house music in training

Maresca looked back to last September when goalkeeper Robert Sanchez was dismissed after only five minutes for former side Chelsea at the same venue - a defeat which he referenced after Sunday's game.

The manager was forced into changes that evening and appeared to panic by making two substitutions in the opening seven minutes, effectively moving his side to a back five but unable to see the game out.

Fast forward one year - his decision to assess the situation before making major changes proved critical, shifting Rayan Cherki to the right, then replacing him at half-time with Iliman Ndiaye was a noteworthy tactical tweak.

"How do you say in English? Happy wife, happy life. For us, happy Erling, happy life," said a beaming Maresca after being asked about Erling Haaland's winner and his contributions this season.

Such jovial remarks from a smiling Maresca in news conferences are in contrast to predecessor Guardiola, who often looked like he would rather be anywhere else but in that chair.

In May, which transpired to be Guardiola's final month at City, the Spaniard was asked what advice he would give the next manager.

"Be themselves," was the reply - and Maresca is beginning to step out of his shadow.

While Guardiola was often leaping and screaming around his technical area during games, Maresca looks to be the opposite as he tends to stand motionless by the pitch with his arms folded.

The most eye-catching change in training has been the introduction of loud house music, which Maresca himself described as the "boom, boom, boom" type - the approach is to make the players feel "more happy" and "work better".

New captain Ruben Dias recently said in a BBC Sport interview that Maresca had introduced his own ideas, but the fundamentals remain as they were under Guardiola.

Dias said: "There's obviously many things from training sessions to some details about the way we press, details about the way we defend that make all of these Enzo's idea.

"It's still a change, of course. Many things have changed, but in some ways continuity in terms of the way we are playing, and there are details that make it different. But still, all very similar to the way we have always behaved at the club."

Guardiola comparisons 'don't put pressure on me'

Maresca's arrival began with the inevitable comparisons of when David Moyes replaced Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013.

The 46-year-old referenced Ferguson and Arsene Wenger in his unveiling news conference, saying clubs "struggled a little bit" after the departures of long-serving managers.

It's almost easy to forget City started this season with a 3-0 defeat at the hands of Arsenal in the Community Shield, but the side have bounced back in style with five straight victories, including the Champions League win at Porto.

While the Old Trafford job appeared to be too much for Moyes to handle, lasting only 10 months before being sacked, Maresca seems to be embracing the "challenge" and "privilege" of succeeding Guardiola.

Maresca acknowledged to reporters in pre-season that City's former boss would be referenced on a regular basis, but batted that particular narrative away by asserting "it doesn't put pressure on me".

The former Chelsea and Leicester manager needed to hit the ground running at Etihad Stadium in order avoid questions about whether he was the right man for the job having been the only person City targeted to take over.

City made major changes in the squad during the summer and the new-look side begin their Carabao Cup defence against Norwich at the Etihad on Thursday (19:30 BST), followed by hosting Sunderland in the Premier League three days later.

Maresca dispatched rivals United on their own turf, and victory in the next two games will ensure a near-perfect start to his tenure in one of football's toughest jobs.

articles.title: Philippe Coutinho joins Neymar at Santos FC until the end of the season
articles.summary: The former Liverpool and Barcelona midfielder joins Brazilian side Santos from his boyhood club Vasco da Gama.
articles.body:
Philippe Coutinho has joined his close friend and Brazil team-mate Neymar at Santos FC until the end of the season.

The former Liverpool and Barcelona midfielder, 34, has been without a club since leaving Vasco da Gama in February.

Coutinho returned to his childhood club in 2024 but left after 81 appearances, saying he was "tired mentally" .

Santos welcomed the player on social media by posting an old photo of Coutinho and Neymar as teenagers, alongside a new version of them re-enacting the pose in the gym.

The club also posted a video of Coutinho walking into the dressing room where he receives a hug from Neymar and says "if it's a dream, I don't want to wake up".

Neymar returned to Santos , his childhood team, in January last year and this will be the first time that the friends have played together at club level.

Coutinho started his career at Vasco before joining Inter Milan and later moving to Liverpool in 2013, where he scored 54 goals in 201 games before joining Barcelona for £142m in 2018.

He later had stints at Bayern Munich, Aston Villa and Al-Duhail before the return to Vasco.

articles.title: El Sevilla crece desde la presión alta
articles.standfirst: Los hispalenses lideran las cinco grandes ligas en recuperaciones cerca del área rival
articles.summary: Los hispalenses lideran las cinco grandes ligas en recuperaciones cerca del área rival
articles.body: Una de las grandes virtudes del Sevilla desde la llegada de Luis García Plaza reside en la presión en campo contrario. "Tenemos que crecer desde el trabajo y desde que corran los de arriba. Han currado y han trabajado el partido", explicaba el entrenador madrileño después de la última victoria de los suyos frente al Valencia, que los coloca con 10 puntos en la clasificación liguera. Los datos no solamente ratifican esta propuesta de juego, sino que de momento están respaldándola con resultados positivos. Según publicó @OptaJose, cuenta oficial de Stats Perform sobre el fútbol español, el Sevilla es el equipo de las cinco grandes ligas europeas que más balones recupera en zona comprometida (53), así como el que realiza un mayor número de presiones (86, superando por 31 acciones a su perseguidor más inmediato). El máximo exponente de esta idea se produjo precisamente ante el Valencia, donde recuperó 17 balones en zona alta, lo que supone el récord en un partido de LaLiga este curso y el cuarto registro más elevado de los hispalenses desde la temporada 2014-15. Esta presión asfixiante que realiza el Sevilla a sus oponentes se sostiene principalmente en los duelos. Tras la quinta jornada, se trata del tercer equipo del campeonato con más duelos ganados (276), siendo superado tan solo por la Real Sociedad (282) y el Racing de Santander (279). Además, el conjunto blanquirrojo lidera el ranking de duelos aéreos junto a Osasuna con 83 disputas ganadas. El trabajo de futbolistas como Isaac Romero o Jon Guridi en la primera línea de presión, el despliegue de Lucien Agoumé y Youssouf Fofana en la medular o el poderío por arriba de Kike Salas, sobre todo al salir de zona, convierten al Sevilla en una máquina de morder que compensa la falta de fluidez en ataque a base de intensidad. Un colmillo que le está permitiendo cimentar su crecimiento desde el esfuerzo colectivo y la solidez del bloque.

articles.title: Roberto Gómez: "Por fin el Real Madrid tiene un portavoz"
articles.standfirst: El periodista elogia la actitud de Mourinho en las ruedas de prensa y destaca que "opina bien" y que sus argumentos son "muy coherentes y muy sensatos"
articles.summary: El periodista elogia la actitud de Mourinho en las ruedas de prensa y destaca que "opina bien" y que sus argumentos son "muy coherentes y muy sensatos"
articles.body: Roberto Gómez tiene claro que el Real Madrid ha encontrado en Mourinho una figura que necesitaba. El colaborador de La Tribu elogió la actitud del entrenador en sus comparecencias ante los medios y destacó su papel como portavoz del club. "El Madrid necesitaba un portavoz. Hasta ahora, el portavoz del Real Madrid en los últimos tiempos era Real Madrid Televisión, sobre todo con el tema de los árbitros. Es lo único que sabíamos del Real Madrid", afirmó Roberto Gómez. Para el colaborador, Mourinho está ofreciendo algo más en sus ruedas de prensa. "Pero es que opina, y opina bien", señaló. Y explicó el motivo de su valoración: "Cada uno de los argumentos que dan son muy coherentes y muy sensatos. A mí me gusta mucho". Roberto Gómez fue todavía más contundente al valorar las comparecencias del técnico: "A mí me gustaría que todos los entrenadores y que la mayoría estuvieran en la rueda de prensa como está en este momento Mourinho. A mí me parece un espectáculo". Durante la conversación con Raúl Varela, Roberto Gómez también destacó la evolución que percibe en Mourinho. "Es un Mourinho más pausado, más maduro, más reflexivo", apuntó. Y volvió a resumir su opinión sobre el papel que está desempeñando en el Real Madrid: "Es un Mourinho que le viene muy bien al Real Madrid. Por fin el Real Madrid tiene un portavoz". Raúl Varela también salió al paso de las quejas del portugués por la cantidad de ruedas de prensa y recordó que Mourinho ya vivía una situación similar en Portugal. "Eso ya lo hacía en Portugal", afirmó. Gómez también valoró que el técnico pueda pronunciarse sobre diferentes asuntos relacionados con la actualidad futbolística. "Opina de todo. Lo mismo del Balón de Oro que opina de los árbitros", señaló.

articles.title: Liverpool under Andoni Iraola need to play three games a week but can they do it playing his pressing game effectively?
articles.summary: Liverpool have made an unbeaten start to life under Andoni Iraola but one win from four Premier League games and a sluggish showing at home to Fulham raises questions too; Adam Bate looks at the challenge that comes with increasing the intensity levels
articles.body:
He added: "I have to learn who is ready to play every two or three days and who is ready to rest so their performance level doesn't drop. I had an idea with some of them, but for some of them it is new as they have not played as many games and we are learning."

Iraola found out some of those answers on Saturday afternoon at Anfield as Liverpool played out a disappointing stalemate against a Fulham team that had lost their first three matches. The midweek fixture against Atletico Madrid in Europe clearly had an impact.

"A lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it," he insisted afterwards. Iraola talked of it being "the worst turnaround" in terms of the hours permitted under the Premier League regulations but acknowledged that Liverpool will need to learn to deal with it.

"This is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe. But sometimes it is going to happen the same way during the season." A cursory glance at the forthcoming fixture list reveals some obvious concerns if this is going to be a problem in the future.

Immediately after the upcoming international break, Iraola's side host Manchester City in what is likely to be a demanding game before travelling to Austria to play LASK Linz in the Champions League. Inside 72 hours they are back in action away to Brentford.

The following month, another massive home match against Arsenal is followed up by a midweek trip to Fenerbahce before Liverpool return to play Crystal Palace away. Later in November, a visit to Club Brugge is sandwiched between Manchester United and Everton.

This is the reality of the demands at a top team. The great unknown for Iraola was always going to be how his players would respond to the challenge of embracing the hard-running style that is fundamental to his approach while maintaining high standards.

"I am asking them to do things that are a little bit different, especially without the ball and I think they are trying to get it," said Iraola in pre-season. Alexander Isak referenced it after the friendly against Monaco. "We are all working hard to make things work."

But the game against Fulham was the first real examination of what happens when the two worlds collide. A draining Champions League night at Anfield in which Liverpool had to come from behind to win was followed by a fixture where they had to force the pace.

Iraola is always lucid in his analysis and identified the problem when speaking in the press conference after the game. "Especially in the first half, we were arriving late to the presses." Tactical corrections were made at the interval but the issue was not fully resolved.

Liverpool's tendency to become a split team - the defence retreating while the attackers press - has been a feature thus far. Against Fulham, there were times when Josh King and others were able to enjoy a surprising amount of space in the gaps that opened up.

It was a problem when the press failed and Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno was able to find an easy pass out, taking multiple Liverpool forwards out of the game. Far from ideal but Iraola is highly unlikely to discourage his players from committing to this pressing.

Passes allowed per defensive action (PPDA) are a popular proxy for calculating a team's pressing habits. Liverpool's PPDA currently stands at just 8.6 so far this season. It is early in the campaign but that is even lower than any full season under Jurgen Klopp.

It was higher than average against Fulham, perhaps an indication that players were, as Iraola suggests, a little off the usual pace. Nevertheless, Liverpool have made the most sprints in the Premier League this season and are up 12 places for total distance covered.

They are running more, sprinting more and pressing more. It is one of the reasons why Iraola was brought in. There was a demand to return to this brand of football. Now the task is to ensure that Liverpool can do it effectively every time. That is more difficult.

Iraola has made attempts to freshen it up. The plan seems to be to rotate the wingers, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister too. But Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz were asked to go again against Fulham and neither hit the levels of three days earlier.

Wirtz, in particular, was sloppy in his use of the ball and some supporters are not so keen to keep making excuses for a player who came with a big reputation. Is work-rate a mitigating factor? Wirtz ranks second in the league for distance covered at high speeds.

He could be one of those referred to when Iraola talks of finding out who can play every three days. "You can put the same players in every game," he conceded on Monday. "The problem is there will be a moment they are very tired and there is more risk of injury."

With Hugo Ekitike unavailable, Liverpool can ill afford that to happen to Isak, for example. Is the Swedish striker even a natural pressing forward anyway? The same might be said of Iraola's midfielders. Time to trust Trey Nyoni? A role for the experienced Wataru Endo?

As Iraola himself points out, this is a learning process - and he is in uncharted territory. The question of how he would navigate three games in a week was always the big one for a popular and skilled coach. Now, the job for the Liverpool boss is to find the answers.

articles.title: Erling Haaland’s Man City goal decision vs Man Utd an ‘error of judgement', says Pro Ref
articles.summary: Refereeing body Pro Ref admits "error of judgment" in awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd; Pro Ref has contacted Man Utd and revealed Erling Haaland's goal "should have recommended an on-field review"; Haaland's second-half winner secured a 1-0 win for 10-man Man City at Old Trafford
articles.body:
In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.

Sky Sports News understands United have received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision. However, United will take no further action with Pro Ref despite remaining hugely frustrated by the situation. United have appreciated the effort Howard Webb and ProRef have made to apologise and explain the mistake.

The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Despite not touching the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to impact the defending of Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez before Haaland's back-post finish, which by the laws of the game should have led to the goal remaining disallowed.

A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

In their post on X explaining why the goal was awarded, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: 'VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball.'

That stress on Fernandez not playing the ball chimed with replays shown during the VAR review, in which the VAR officials apparently sought to detect whether or not the City midfielder played the ball.

However, the offside rule clearly stipulates that a player can be offside despite not playing the ball and can interfere with an opponent by:

preventing an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing the opponent's line of vision or

clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent or

making an obvious action which clearly impacts on the ability of an opponent to play the ball

Speaking at the time of the goal on co-commentary, Sky Sports' Gary Neville believed the VAR officials were "wrong" to award Haaland's effort.

Pro Ref's statement, however, fell short of Neville's prediction that they would apologise.

The former Man Utd defender told Sky Sports : "We will see an apology from Pro Ref.

"There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off.

"It's a really strange one. They'll recognise they got that wrong."

Speaking on his podcast, Neville continued: "I think they are ignoring the rule.

"They are digging themselves a bigger hole [with the Match Centre statement]. I'm really surprised they put that out.

Meanwhile, Man Utd defender Martinez said in his post-match interview that the goal should not have stood.

He told Sky Sports : "Every season the officials come to our club and spend an hour explaining the rules and they look so confident with that.

"Then after, five or six people [officials] doing this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable.

"We have to go home with this injustice."

Former Man City defender Micah Richards dismissed Match Centre's explanation that the goal was awarded because Fernandez didn't touch the ball as a "nonsense".

Asked whether Fernandez was clearly attempting to play the ball, Richards told Sky Sports : "One hundred per cent he is.

"I think it's been a bad day for referees and VAR.

"They got the Phil Foden decision wrong , and they got this decision wrong.

"How you can not say Enzo Fernandez is challenging for the ball - of course he is!

"I've been in that position as a defender where any slight movement can make the difference for going for the ball or not, so of course it affects him.

Roy Keane concluded: "Fernandez is interfering with play. Basically, United have been punished for holding a good line. When you are in that position, you are impacting the game. You're in the middle of the box, you're going for the ball.

"Their line is good. Fernandez is offside, and he goes to play the ball, so United are getting punished for good defending."

Carragher: 'It's a bad one from officials'

Jamie Carragher also admitted that the decision to allow Haaland's goal to stand was "a bad one."

Speaking ahead of Monday Night Football, the former Liverpool defender said: "It's a bad one. We all look at it and it looks offside. Haaland looks offside but we know he's not. Then when you break it down, it is poor from the officials.

"It seems to me they've become obsessed with Haaland being onside. They haven't gone into as much detail with Fernandez in the middle and understanding of his impact on it."

The incident drew comparisons of the mistake that occurred when Luis Diaz and Liverpool saw a goal wrongly ruled out for offside against Tottenham, where the VAR process showed the Colombian to be onside.

Carragher believes that remains the worse of the two VAR mistakes.

"I suppose Liverpool's one was more of a communication error and understanding the process of what they should be doing," he added.

"What happened yesterday was a huge error and it was a huge game. One of the biggest games not just in our league, but around the world. There was only one goal in the game which makes it feel worse.

"I think it's different to the Liverpool one because you don't expect that not to be a goal. They confirm it's a goal, really. I'm still going for the Liverpool one [being worse]."

articles.title: 'Operación Intercontinental' en La Fábrica: 20 campeones de la Youth y tres 'fichajes'
articles.standfirst: Este martes empieza ya a entrenarse junto el equipo sub 20 del Real Madrid que disputará la final por el título mundial el sábado en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: Este martes empieza ya a entrenarse junto el equipo sub 20 del Real Madrid que disputará la final por el título mundial el sábado en el Bernabéu
articles.body: El sábado se juega una final en el Bernabéu (12.30 horas). Está en juego la Intercontinental sub 20 que enfrentará al Real Madrid, como campeón de la Youth League, y al Santiago Wanderers chileno, ganador de la Libertadores sub 20. Un título con el que La Fábrica cerraría un círculo histórico logrando el único trofeo que falta en las vitrinas de la cantera de Valdebebas. Cinco meses después de proclamarse rey de Europa, el Madrid juvenil podría ser rey del Mundo. Un logro que desde hace tiempo centra la atención en La Fábrica madridista, que se paralizará este fin de semana pensando en la finalísima del Bernabéu. Por ello se han aplazado los partidos de sus tres primeros filiales, Castilla, Real Madrid C y Juvenil A, donde juegan todos los canteranos que eran seleccionables para el histórico compromiso ante el Santiago Wanderers, que podrán disputar los nacidos desde el 1 de enero de 2006. De entre todos ellos hay una previsión de 23 jugadores (tres porteros y 20 futbolistas de campo) con prioridad para los héroes de la Youth League, cuyo núcleo permanece casi intacto en Valdebebas repartidos en su mayoría entre el Castilla y el Madrid C. Las únicas ausencias serán las de Jacobo Ortega y Valdepeñas, que salieron en verano. A partir de ahí, lesiones, estados de forma (Melvin y Barroso han arrastrado lesiones), apuestas estratégicas en determinados posiciones (Yeremaiah se puede colar en la lista) y fichajes nuevos (Fran Santamaría y Sergio Martínez) pueden marcar la confección definitiva de la convocatoria de 23 jugadores. Thiago Pitarch sería la guinda a la 'selección sub 20' de La Fábrica, pero su presencia está en el aire. Un 'grupo de élite' con 20 campeones de la Youth y tres 'fichajes' que desde este martes trabajará junto, al margen de los otros filiales, en una concentración de cuatro días y dando forma a una 'selección sub 20' inédita para un sólo partido. Una reunión galáctica de talento en busca de un título que hace mucha ilusión en Valdebebas. Una colección de 'joyas' que estará a las órdenes de Álvaro López, el técnico que llevó al juvenil del Real Madrid a la gloria europea la pasada temporada después de asumir las riendas del equipo en enero. Desde entonces ha ganado Youth League, Liga y Copa de Campeones. Por ello en Valdebebas se le conoce como 'SuperLópez'. La Intercontinental le consolidaría en las historia de los banquillos de La Fábrica. Portero: Javi Navarro, Illia y Álvaro González. Defensas: Fortea, Bailón, Joan Martínez, Ariel, Mario Rivas, Aguado, Lezcano y Liberto. Medios: Cestero, Lacosta, Roberto Martín, Sergio Martínez, Beto, Carlos Díez y Adri Pérez. Delanteros: Yáñez, Ciria, Gabri Valero, Yeremaiah y Santamaría.

articles.title: El hijo futbolista de un mito publica su test toxicológico tras ser acusado de dar positivo en drogas y alcohol
articles.standfirst: Daniel Maldini, el hijo de Paolo Maldini, trata de demostrar que no dio positivo por drogas tras su accidente de tráfico
articles.summary: Daniel Maldini, el hijo de Paolo Maldini, trata de demostrar que no dio positivo por drogas tras su accidente de tráfico
articles.body: Daniel Maldini, jugador del Cagliari e hijo del mítico Paolo Maldini, se defiende en las redes sociales tras ser acusado de dar positivo en drogas y alcohol tras un accidente de tráfico con su coche (Porsche Carrera 4 ) en Milán. La prensa italiana publicó que el futbolista registró valores de 0,91 mg/l en la primera prueba y 0,89 mg/l en la segunda, realizadas en el lugar de los hechos por la policía local, cuando el máximo permitido por ley en Italia es 0,5 /g/l). Daniel Maldini ha publicado en su cuenta de Instagram los resultados negativos del test toxicológico para acallar rumores sobre el positivo por drogas. El diario 'La Gazzetta dello Sport' informa que el resultado de la prueba procede de un centro de Cagliari, adonde Maldini regresó tras recibir el alta hospitalaria. El resultado negativo ya había sido comunicado previamente por el Cagliari. "Nadie discute que Daniel cometió un error de juicio, pero hay errores y luego están los "errores". La gente debe tener cuidado con lo que escribe y con los titulares sensacionalistas que crea. Hace falta más cuidado y respeto. Siempre hay un empeño en buscar una historia sensacionalista para ponerlo en una situación comprometida. Daniel es uno de los pocos talentos auténticos que tenemos", declaró su agente Beppe Riso. Daniel Maldini (24 años) ya se entrena con normalidad con el Cagliari en el Crai Sport Center de Assemini.

articles.title: Canales: "El Barça quería ficharme. Vi La Masia y me enamoré"
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista recuerda cuando estuvo a punto de ser azulgrana pero finalmente acabó fichando por le Real Madrid
articles.summary: El centrocampista recuerda cuando estuvo a punto de ser azulgrana pero finalmente acabó fichando por le Real Madrid
articles.body: Sergio Canales pasó por le micrófono del canal de Youtube de Mario Suárez para hablar de sus inicios en el mundo del fútbol profesional y desveló lo cerca que estuvo de fichar por el Barça. El jugador acabó en el Real Madrid, camiseta que vistió entre 2010 y 2012, pero todo pudo cambiar poco antes, cuando el futbolista visitó las instalaciones azulgranas: "El Barça quería ficharme. Fui con mis padres a La Masia y quería quedarme. Vi las instalaciones y me enamoré. Pero ellos tenían su vida aquí (Santander) y dijeron que no podían hipotecar todo". Es por eso que no se pudo dar fichaje por el cuadro azulgrana y terminó, en 2010, en el Real Madrid. "Mi primera opción era ir cedido, pero cuando llega Mou me piden que haga la pretemporada. Juego de titular en Mallorca y aun así llamo para salir cedido. Al final no se da y piensan que tengo que estar. No me arrepiento porque me ayudó a crecer mentalmente", recordaba Canales en 'El camino de Mario'. El centrocampista recordó también su relación con el que vuelve a ser entrenador madridista: "A Mourinho le estoy agradecido en cierto modo. Él con los jugadores jóvenes, creía que siendo duro los hacía más fuertes. Fue una experiencia que me ha ayudado a madurar". A su lado tenía grandes figuras de talla mundial de los que quiso aprender todo: "Hubo un momento en el que dije: 'Me voy a fichar en qué hace Cristiano, Xabi Alonso, Arbeloa...'. Yo no había tocado un gimnasio en mi vida. Antes de jugar con el Racing iba al cine y me comía tres bolsas de palomitas y acababa el partido y una hamburguesa. Estar rodeado de los mejores del mundo te hace ver cómo es la previa y el post. Acabo ese año y quería un nutricionista, un preparador físico y ese verano me cambia la mente".

articles.title: Premier League: What are the yellow card suspension rules and which players have the most?
articles.summary: A look at what the Premier League's rules are for players who receive too many yellow cards during the season
articles.body:
Premier League players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

From the first four rounds of Premier League matches this term, three players have already received three bookings. It means that they must avoid getting two more yellow cards prior to the halfway point of the season.

After that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From then, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

For players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with all three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the regular season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

articles.title: "¿Existe alguien en Madrid que piense que lo de Diomande puede ser un fracaso?"
articles.standfirst: Emilio Pérez de Rozas no entiende la situación que está viviendo el fichaje del Real Madrid tras el precio que pagaron por él
articles.summary: Emilio Pérez de Rozas no entiende la situación que está viviendo el fichaje del Real Madrid tras el precio que pagaron por él
articles.body: Ramón Álvarez de Mon, Emilio Pérez de Rozas, Jorge Liaño, Pepe Pasqués, José Rodríguez, Javi Lázaro y Alberto Santacruz han sido los tertulianos de este martes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada un día más por la carrera por el Balón de Oro y la nueva jornada de LaLiga. Ramón Álvarez de Mon. "Veo a un Barcelona haciendo muchos puntos en LaLiga, es muy superior a la mayoría de equipos". Emilio Pérez de Rozas. "Lo de Diomande es un tema que podría explicar Mourinho. ¿No os parece flipante que haya jugado 12 minutos costando 140 millones? El Real Madrid ha fichado, según todos los voceros del reino, a la estrella mundial de los mundiales, al tipo que se va con la mirada... y eso no está mirando. ¿Existe alguien en Madrid que piense que lo de Diomande puede ser un fracaso?". Jorge Liaño. "No es que los clubes españoles no quieran vender al Real Madrid, la realidad es que el Real Madrid no quiere comprar a los clubes españoles". Pepe Pasqués. "Hay jugadores que vienen de otros sistemas y les lleva más tiempo interpretar lo que les busca". José Rodríguez. "No puedes castigar a Mourinho por el precio, él no es el que toma de decisión de pagarlo. Aquí y en todos los sitios hay alguien da el visto bueno para pagar ese precio. Cada caso es individual. Baena cuando llega se lesiona dos veces: de los primeros 14 partidos es titular 10". Javi Lázaro. "¿El Madrid vende barato? Cuando tiene salidas, vende caro. El debate es si el Madrid con las necesidades que tienen no podría haber invertido ese dinero mejor". Alberto Santacruz. "¿Para qué existen las cláusulas de rescisión? Si hay un equipo que piden hasta su último euro por su filosofía es al Athletic y al Real Madrid que va de dueño fubolístico, pues hace lo mismo".

articles.title: El acierto total de Rodri con el Barça
articles.standfirst: Sus números y aportaciones ya son determinantes
articles.summary: Sus números y aportaciones ya son determinantes
articles.body: Rodri fue una de las sorpresas del mercado de verano azulgrana. El centrocampista madrileño apostó por salir del City y su primera opción de destino era el Barça, por lo que el club catalán se lanzó a por su incorporación, aunque a priori reforzar la medular no era una prioridad, seguro de que su liderazgo y cualidades iban a implicar un impulso competitivo para el equipo de Hansi Flick. Y lo está siendo. El internacional español, de 30 años, se ha adaptado en tiempo récord al Barcelona. El centrocampista, que firmó hasta 2030, entró de forma progresiva al equipo. Después de disputar 27 y 26 minutos respectivamente contra el Athletic y el Rayo, en las primeras jornadas, encadena tres encuentros de titular: salió de inicio en LaLiga contra el Valencia y el Levante y frente al Feyenoord en la Champions League. Su rendimiento ha sido más que destacado, hasta ser magistral este pasado fin de semana, en el encuentro en el Ciutat de València. Sus números no dejan lugar a dudas. Fue el jugador que dio más toques: 131. Pero, además, completó el 95 por ciento de las combinaciones (111/117), destacando un éxito del cien por cien en las largas (12/12) y en las realizadas en el tercio final (11/11). Así mismo, fue el centrocampista con más intervenciones defensivas (9) y el que más duelos ganó (7), y tuvo un acierto absoluto en descargas precisas (4/4)... "Estamos muy contentos de que esté en nuestro equipo y se puede ver todo lo que hace con la pelota y también sin el balón. Nos da estructura. Todo lo que hace en el terreno de juego tiene sentido", comentó Flick hace unos días. Pero, además, Rodri, que ganó el regate que probó contra los granotas, no sólo fue clave en el control del balón y en la recuperación (rescató 8 balones y tuvo dos intercepciones), también ganó metros y dio dos toques en el área rival. Rodri, por otro lado, ha mostrado su capacidad de adaptarse a distintos compañeros, y su nivel ha sido excelso tanto cuando ha compartido minutos con Pedri, que es con el que más ha jugado, como Marc Bernal. Pero Flick no sólo le considera una pieza fundamental en su esquema por todas estas cualidades. El técnico alemán apostó de inmediato por su fichaje, la operación con el City se cerró en 60 millones de euros fijos más 16,5 en variables, también por su capacidad de liderazgo. La veteranía, ascendencia en el grupo, voz de mando, responsabilidad y profesionalidad que siempre ha mostrado el veterano futbolista madrileño son características muy valoradas por el preparador y que impulsaron, aún más, la llegada de internacional al Spotify Camp Nou. "Rodri es increíble, no solo en el césped, también en el vestuario. Es un líder absoluto, y es genial tenerlo", ha repetido el preparador, satisfecho, en varias ocasiones. En el Barça están orgullosos de su fichaje.

articles.title: Europa League: Why are there nine league phase fixtures on Wednesday?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why there are nine Europa League matches taking place on Wednesday night
articles.body:
The opening round of league phase matches in the 2026-27 Europa League campaign start on Wednesday evening, a day earlier than the competition's usual slot.

Typically, fixtures in both the Europa League and Conference League are played on Thursday nights. Some exceptions are made during the season in scenarios where fixture clashes with other European matches in a similar geographical area means games can be rescheduled.

But on Wednesday, nine of the 18 games scheduled in match week one of the Europa League's league phase are taking place.

The other nine will be played on Thursday during the Europa League's dedicated game week of the season.

Sunderland, AC Milan, Benfica and Lyon are among the teams that are in action on Wednesday.

The Champions League also has an exclusive week, which takes place in the opening round of fixtures.

Last week saw games in Europe's top tier league taking place across Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

The Conference League also gets its own designated week. However, this takes place in December in the final round of league phase matches.

This first happened in the 2024-25 season when, like the Champions League and Conference League, the competition was reformatted into a league phase system.

articles.title: Nations League: Injured Joe Rodon and Dylan Lawlor are absent as Wales call up Cian Ashford
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy hands a first call-up to Cardiff City forward Cian Ashford for Wales' Nations League A campaign but is without key defender Joe Rodon.
articles.body:
Craig Bellamy has handed a first call-up to Cardiff City forward Cian Ashford for Wales' return to the top flight of the Nations League but is without key defender Joe Rodon to take on Erling Haaland and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Wales face Portugal, Denmark and Norway in League A of the competition, but will do so without first-choice centre-back Rodon who has been ruled out with a hamstring injury.

Defensive partner Dylan Lawlor is also missing from the 28-man squad - he is yet to appear this season because of a knee problem - as is fellow Cardiff defender Ronan Kpakio.

Leeds United's Harry Wilson and Wolves midfielder Jordan James return to the squad after missing June's friendlies with Ghana and Romania through injury, as does Swansea City defender Ben Cabango.

As well as returns for Mark Harris and Liam Cullen, there is a recall for 10-cap winger Wes Burns, now of Leicester City, who could make his first international appearance since 2024.

Wales travel to face Portugal on 24 September in the first of four fixtures in this newly extended international break, with a home match against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway sandwiched by two games with Denmark.

Captain Ben Davies retains his place having been named in the squad for the summer games without featuring.

The 33-year-old defender had not played since a serious ankle injury suffered with Tottenham in January, but has since returned to action for Spurs and is in contention for his first international appearance since October 2025 when he won his 100th cap.

Ashford, 21, gets his chance having impressed in the early stages of the Championship season, as part of attacking options that also include Liverpool's Lewis Koumas.

Fellow Cardiff forwards Isaak Davies and Rubin Colwill are unavailable for selection because of injury, while there is no place for midfielder Kai Andrews despite his impressive start at Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United on loan from Coventry City.

Wales' opponents are yet to name their squads, although Cristiano Ronaldo is expected to be selected for Portugal in their first games under his former Saudi Pro League club boss, Jorge Jesus.

The games are the first since manager Bellamy was close to leaving his national post after holding talks with Championship club Burnley.

The 78-cap former striker has seen two key members of his backroom staff leave their roles in the meantime, with number two Piet Cremers taking a job in Belgium and assistant coach James Rowberry opting to focus on club duties as assistant manager at Stoke City.

They will be replaced on Bellamy's coaching staff by former captain Ashley Williams and ex-Swansea City boss Alan Sheehan in what is expected to be a challenging period for Wales.

Without a win in their past four games, these are the first competitive fixtures since a penalty shoot-out defeat by Bosnia-Herzegovina in March's play-offs cost Wales a place in the World Cup.

Wales have not beaten a side in the top 20 of the world rankings since a 2-1 win over Croatia in October 2023 - and are yet to beat a side ranked higher than themselves under Bellamy.

Now they face that challenge in quick succession, starting with prospect of current Nations League holders Portugal.

Wales - who are 38th in the world rankings, their lowest position since August 2014 - then travel to Copenhagen to take on a Denmark side ranked 21st in the world before the visit of World Cup quarter-finalists Norway to Cardiff (1 October) and the return game with Denmark (4 October).

articles.title: Maresca se ‘desmarca’ de Guardiola: “Estoy aquí para hacer mi trabajo a mi manera”
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico del Manchester City se ha repuesto de la contundente derrota frente al Arsenal en la Community Shield firmando un 12/12 para arrancar la Premier
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico del Manchester City se ha repuesto de la contundente derrota frente al Arsenal en la Community Shield firmando un 12/12 para arrancar la Premier
articles.body: La elección de Enzo Maresca por parte de Hugo Viana y la dirección deportiva del Manchester City correspondía a la apuesta por una línea continuista —fue asistente en la temporada 22-23 que acabó en triplete— respecto a la década dorada protagonizada por Pep Guardiola. El técnico italiano, sin embargo, quiere ‘desmarcarse’ de la figura de su ‘mentor’ para escribir su propia historia en el Etihad… y el triunfo ante el United en el ‘Derby of Manchester’ fue su primera gran tarde como técnico ‘skyblue’. “No creo en el ‘copy and paste’. Cada entrenador es diferente y puede aportar algo distinto. Es mi objetivo y mi deber introducir algunas cosas nuevas”, recalcó Maresca durante la pretemporada. “Estoy aquí para hacer mi trabajo a mi manera, no para tratar de copiar a alguien. Estoy aquí para implantar mi fútbol y mi idea”. Siempre, eso sí, mostrando un profundo respeto hacia Guardiola. El verano, seguro, fue mucho más agitado de lo que se podía llegar a intuir. Las salidas de Rodri, Marmoush, Nico González, Savinho… derivaron en un mercado récord en ventas. Les costó reaccionar tras adelantarse en el fichaje de Elliot Anderson —también llegó Rulli— previo a la disputa del Mundial. Sin embargo, la contundente derrota frente al Arsenal en la Community Shield encendió la voz de alarma. “Tenemos bastante claro lo que tenemos que hacer”, apuntó. ‘Aceleraron’ durante la recta final elevando el gasto hasta los 526 millones para hacerse con Enzo Fernández, Bouadi, Ndiaye y Allan. “Uno de los grandes éxitos de este club ha sido reemplazar a sus grandes jugadores. Eso no es fácil. Antes con Txiki Begiristain y ahora con Hugo Viana. Me siento muy afortunado”, reconoció un Enzo Maresca que confesó sentirse “muy contento por el esfuerzo de la propiedad”, recalcando que, ahora sí, era “momento de trabajar”. Lo prometido era deuda… y el arranque en Premier está siendo impecable: han firmado un pleno de puntos (12/12) en las cuatro primeras jornadas —también ganaron en Champions frente al Oporto— y la victoria en Old Trafford reflejó que Maresca eleva la competitividad en escenarios de exigencia máxima. Reaccionó a la temprana expulsión de Foden, resistieron al arreón ‘red devil’ en el inicio del segunda tiempo, Haaland dejó su sello en uno de los pocos balones que tocó y terminaron mostrando madurez para conservar el resultado. “Cambió el plan para nosotros, pero también para ellos. Son increíbles en transición y en el momento en que nos quedamos con 10 no les dimos ninguna transición. El plan táctico es una cosa, pero lo principal hoy fue el esfuerzo de los jugadores, excepcional”, recalcó después del choque. Desde luego, puede estar orgulloso. Más allá de Guardiola, que lo logró tres veces, ha igualado los arranques de Roberto Mancini (11-12) y Manuel Pellegrini (15-16). Maresca, poco a poco, va conociendo mejor a su nueva plantilla y está empezando a encontrar su once tipo. El esquema base siempre parte de un 1-4-2-3-1. Pero, en la práctica, ‘muta’ en una especie de 1-3-4-3 con un rombo en el centro del campo. Los actores, sin embargo, han ido cambiando con el paso de los partidos. Nunes, que firmó una actuación colosal ante el United, ha entrado en el flanco derecho de la defensa en lugar de Khusanov para aportar mayor profundidad. En consecuencia, Gvardiol cierra en línea de tres y Foden, aunque arranque de banda, tiene libertad para juntarse dentro con Anderson, Enzo y Cherki. La roja directa que vio el propio Foden ante el United, la cual acarrea un castigo de tres partidos, obligará a Maresca a recalcular el plan antes y después del primer parón del curso. Con Doku todavía ausente, puede volver a apostar por una pareja de extremos más puros como Ndiaye y Semenyo… pero también debería modificar el perfil de sus laterales. Otra, manteniendo la idea, es mover a Cherki a banda y que Bouaddi entre en la sala de máquinas. Variantes, desde luego, tiene para mantenerle el paso al Arsenal.

articles.title: Cyle Larin: Southampton's 'Brampton bagsman' is taking the Championship by storm
articles.summary: BBC Sport takes a look at the scintillating form of Southampton's 'Brampton bagsman' Cyle Larin.
articles.body:
Not many forwards in world football have had a better start to their season than Southampton's Cyle Larin.

The Canada striker is the leading goalscorer in the Championship and has netted more than anyone in Europe's top five leagues.

He may have played more games than the stars from the Premier League and La Liga, but his seven goals in seven league matches have caught the eye.

His average of 73 minutes per goal is better than the 75 Kylian Mbappe is averaging for Real Madrid and Erling Haaland's 90 minutes per strike in the Premier League for Manchester City.

Larin's exploits have even led Saints head coach Tonda Eckert to label him "the best striker in the league" - lofty praise in a division that also boasts Jarrod Bowen, Raul Jimenez, Mohamed Toure and the emerging Will Lankshear.

But it is just not favouritism from his manager - neutral plaudits, including August's Championship Player of the Month award, are also landing at his feet.

The 'Brampton bagsman' - a nickname coined from his Ontario hometown - has helped propel Eckert's team from bottom of the table on minus four points to inside the top eight with 10.

Saints would be second, behind West Ham on goal difference, if not for the points deduction that came as punishment for the Spygate scandal.

But after a nomadic career that has taken in spells in the United States, Turkey, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands, why has Larin been so effective for the south coast side?

Since signing for Southampton on an initial loan from Mallorca in early 2026, Larin's first venture into English football has been an impactful one.

The 31-year-old netted three minutes into his Saints debut last season, going on to finish with eight Championship goals in 16 games during the second half of the campaign.

Following the fall-out from Spygate, he did not get the chance to help Southampton reach the Premier League but had to quickly turn his attention to the World Cup and representing his country as one of the host nations.

He shone for Canada on the biggest of stages, scoring two goals - one a crucial late equaliser against Bosnia-Herzegovina - as Jesse Marsch's side reached the last 16 before losing to Morocco.

Larin's contribution for Canada as their second all-time leading goalscorer has even earned him a key to his home city of Brampton, , external something he will collect during the upcoming international break.

Back on English soil, Larin has been even more prolific for Saints than he was last term, scoring eight times in nine appearances across all competitions.

However, the forward has been quick to point out it has been far from a solo effort.

"It feels good but I don't think I can do this without my team-mates," he told BBC Radio Solent after scoring twice in the 4-1 win over Bristol City on Saturday.

"They play such a big role in me being able to score and I have to give credit to the coach too, he's given me the role to play free up there and that's what I'm doing.

"It's the beginning of the season and we have to keep working hard as we have a long way to go. You can't get too high after these games, you have to be level-headed."

Larin has a point - in Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza, who boast five goals and six assists between them already this term, he has two of the division's best creators a striker could wish for.

Last season, he shared the minutes up front with Ross Stewart but with the Scot now at Swansea and Larin clearly the first choice at St Mary's, he has been taking advantage of more minutes on the pitch.

Larin rarely completes 90 minutes with Eckert tending to prefer to withdraw him during the second half - and that makes his statistics even more impressive.

He is averaging 1.23 goals per 90 minutes, scoring every 73 minutes with a goal conversion rate of 25% - seven goals from 28 shots.

Only one other striker - Norwich's Mathias Kvistgaarden (1.27) - has a better goal per 90 minutes rate and only Bowen (29) has attempted more shots.

"When you have quality footballers like Larin then you get goals," former Saints midfielder Jo Tessem said on the latest episode of BBC Radio Solent's Goin' Home.

"Quality players like him step up when you need them and so far this season he's done that.

"Eckert has said that Larin has been a lot fitter right now than when he arrived in January and that has made a difference so far."

'Low touch, high impact' - why Larin is so effective

There's a simplicity to Cyle Larin's game - and understanding that has underpinned Southampton's strong start to the campaign.

Rarely tasked with dropping into the build-up, he hangs on the opposition's last line, ready to make powerful runs into the channels.

Tonda Eckert has asked fans to trust Saints when they build from the back, with Larin's movement a significant reason why.

If his team-mates play through the press, he has the space to stretch defences and finish off swift counter attacks.

Larin has stressed the help of his team-mates too.

The immediacy of his runs creates the room for Azaz between the lines and for the combinations between the pair that preceded Larin's opening goal against Bristol City, for example.

Finding space in crowded situations, though - especially for a side who want to dominate possession - is equally crucial for a centre-forward.

Larin's instinctive movement and clever body usage offer a potent mix of snappy shots off either foot, aerial threat and those tricks of the trade the 31-year-old has picked up over the years.

A Larin trademark is drifting to the back post, a magnet for the crossing quality of right-back James Bree.

He is low touch, high impact - but that's just the system Eckert wants around his main man.

articles.title: Javier Aguirre, una opción "posible" para el Valencia
articles.standfirst: El Valencia ya ha contactado con el entorno del entrenador mexicano para ver opciones
articles.summary: El Valencia ya ha contactado con el entorno del entrenador mexicano para ver opciones
articles.body: El Valencia busca entrenador y Javier Aguirre es una opción "posible", según ha podido saber MARCA. De hecho, ya se han producido los primeros contactos entre el entorno del 'Vasco' y el club valencianista. Esto no quiere decir que vaya a ser el entrenador cien por cien, pues debe haber negociación y aceptación por las partes, pero hay que recordar que Javier siempre ve con buenos ojos entrenar en La Liga, competición en la que ya ha tenido seis experiencias: Osasuna, Atlético, Espanyol, Zaragoza, Leganés y Mallorca, con éxito en muchos de ellos. Las primeras 'pláticas' (permítase el término mexicano) están ya en curso, si bien no hay prisa puesto que el Valencia, en ningún caso, sentaría al nuevo entrenador, sea quien sea, en el partido del próximo domingo en casa ante la Real (obviamente, hoy tampoco ante el Alavés) y dejaría ya la transición para después del parón internacional. Además, Aguirre vive ahora mismo fuera de España tras su exitoso Mundial con la Selección de México, cayendo en octavos con Inglaterra. El nuevo director deportivo del club, Braulio Vázquez, tenía subrayado al 'Vasco' como candidato para coger la nave valencianista por su carácter, experiencia y compromiso en todas las instituciones en las que ha estado el mexicano. Hay más candidatos, pero Javier Aguirre "es posible", según una fuente autorizada. El 'Vasco', a sus 67 años, no ha dejado de recibir ofertas de distintos equipos y Selecciones tras la Copa del Mundo, entre ellas Ecuador (que acabó fichando al 'Muñeco' Gallardo) y Corea del Sur. Pero Javi se quiso tomar un respiro tras la extenuante experiencia que supuso dirigir al 'Tri' por tercera vez en su tres Mundial (2002, 2010 y 2026). Pero ahora, ya está listo... por si el Valencia le convence.
