articles.title: Laporta: "Es un orgullo inmenso para el Barcelona y para todos los barcelonistas acoger la final"
articles.standfirst: El presidente, ilusionado con la designación del Spotify Camp Nou
articles.summary: El presidente, ilusionado con la designación del Spotify Camp Nou
articles.body: Joan Laporta expresó su ilusión y agradecimiento por la designación del Spotify Camp Nou como sede de la Champions League para 2029. El presidente aseguró que era un gran orgullo y afirmó que este hecho demuestra que el remodelado feudo culé es una referencia a nivel mundial. Este martes por la mañana la UEFA anunció que Spotify Camp Nou acogería la final de la Champions de 2029, imponiéndose de esta forma a la otra candidata: Wembley. "Es un orgullo inmenso para el FC Barcelona y para todos los barcelonistas", afirmó el presidente culé nada más conocerse la noticia. "Esta elección es también un reconocimiento internacional en el nuevo Spotify Camp Nou, que se consolida como un estadio de referencia mundial, a la vanguardia en experiencia, tecnología, conectividad, accesibilidad y servicios", añadió el abogado catalán. El estadio finalizará durante esta temporada las obras de la tercera gradería y los palcos VIP y el próximo verano empezará los trabajos con la cubierta. Joan Laporta, además, sacó pecho de una de las grandes decisiones tomadas por al junta: la remodelación de un estadio que ya estaba obsoleto. "La confianza de la UEFA para acoger una de las grandes citas del fútbol mundial pone en valor la dimensión y la ambición de este proyecto y consolida al Spotify Camp Nou como un nuevo icono de Barcelona y un referente internacional", dijo. Por último, no se olvidó de las instituciones con las que ha trabajado el Barcelona para poder acoger la final. "Quiero agradecer especialmente al Ayuntamiento de Barcelona, a la Generalitat de Catalunya y a la RFEF su apoyo a esta candidatura. Es un hito que hemos logrado juntos y que proyecta Barcelona, Cataluña y el FC Barcelona en el mundo", concluyó.

articles.title: Oli McBurnie: New Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli recalls striker & names seven uncapped players in squad
articles.summary: Hull City forward Oli McBurnie is called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years while seven uncapped make new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first selection.
articles.body:
Oli McBurnie has been called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years, with new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli saying the Hull City forward fits his "style of play".

Uncapped Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken, Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh also makes Pocognoli's first selection. As expected, Stoke defender Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure receive their first senior call-ups.

Scott Bain, Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and James Wilson are recalled but Che Adams misses out. Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour, 25, returns after missing the World Cup injured.

McBurnie, 30, first featured for his country in 2018 and won the last of his 16 caps in 2021.

He has never scored for Scotland but did net one of the penalties in the shootout that sealed a place at the delayed Euro 2020 finals.

"It's a new opportunity for some players, a really new beginning for the other ones," said Pocognoli.

"I have to start a new journey, start a new book. The most important is regarding the style of play that I want to produce on the pitch. We need to adapt quick.

"To be honest, I can extend this list because I have to make some choices. There are a lot of names who can be also in that squad for that camp. Players who are not there is because for the style of play, it can be from injury or playing time.

"There's many players that I would like to call up. The door is never closed."

Binks, 25, has previously played age grade football for England and Scotland and Pocognoli said in reference to the Brondby player: "The timing was right with him."

Right-back Donovan, 20, has come to prominence filling in for injured Canada right-back Alistair Johnston in Celtic's side this season. Like McBurnie, he has been capped at under-19 and under-21 level. Pocognoli said Donovan had "played some good games" and had dealt with "expectation".

Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.

The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the country's send-off friendly win against Curacao, which was also Steve Clarke's last game in the dugout at Hampden Park.

The defender, who has three caps at under-21 level, has started strongly for The Potters in the Championship, who are unbeaten in their past four games, with Graham an ever-present.

Four-time capped Falkirk goalkeeper Bain, 34, and Bradford City keeper Jon McCracken, 26, were in squads named by Pocognoli's predecessor Clarke. Bain and McCracken join Angus Gunn and Liam Kelly in the goalkeeping pool.

And Pocognoli commented: "I will not talk about my number one and number two today.

"We have a strong generation in the past. Now we need just to rebirth this but we have good quality. We have experienced goalkeepers and we have some young talents."

Pocognoli's compatriot, Heart of Midlothian head coach Wouter Vrancken, was "confident" there would be a few players from the Tynecastle club included and winger McPake, 25, and 19-year-old attacking club-mate James Wilson, who has two caps, are recognised for their early-season performances. However, Hearts winger Calvin Miller misses out.

Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh, 26, may win his first cap while Sassuolo forward Bowie, 23, and left-back Doig, 24, as well as Udinese midfielder Miller, 20, make the cut.

Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - that took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden and it resulted in a £5.5m summer transfer to La Liga with Sevilla.

Ure, 22, has yet to find the target in Spain, but given his eligibility for Ukraine, the new head coach appears tempted to tie him down as soon as possible.

"Players who are there are performing well," said Pocognoli. "Robbie is now challenging to adjust to La Liga level."

The inclusion of Bowie, McBurnie, Ure and Wilson come as reports indicate Torino's Adams is injured while Rangers forward Lawrence Shankland is out for up to four months with a hamstring injury.

Time for Pocognoli to pick - who could be named in new-look Scotland squad?

Stoke best place for me to take step up - Graham

Is Sevilla's 'all-round striker' Ure ready to lead Scotland's attack?

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay, 29, is unavailable, having recently had minor heart surgery.

Of the 28 named in this squad, 14 were part of this summer's World Cup.

Gunn and Kelly, defenders Jack Hendry, Aaron Hickey, Scott McKenna, Nathan Patterson, Andy Robertson and Kieran Tierney, midfielders Ryan Christie, Lewis Ferguson, John McGinn and Kenny McLean and forwards Findlay Curtis and Ben Gannon-Doak are all retained.

Goalkeeper Craig Gordon has retired while Grant Hanley has recently returned to fitness at Hibernian while Rangers defender John Souttar has not played this season amid reports linking him with Aris Thessaloniki.

Defenders Dominic Hyam and Anthony Ralston, midfielder Tyler Fletcher and forwards Lyndon Dykes, George Hirst and Ross Stewart miss out.

When asked about the possibility of calling up Scotland-qualified Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes, 28, and Everton midfielder Hayden Hackney, 24, Pocognoli said he was "aware of everything and about the feeling of everybody" and said "it's about timing."

"I don't want to convince players," he explained. "They need to be open to representing in the natural way, the country. We'll see in the future."

Since Pocognoli was announced as Clarke's successor - the former Kilmarnock manager having resigned after the Scots failed to qualify for the knockout stages of a major tournament for the first time - the expectation was that the Belgian would look to freshen up an ageing squad.

Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in the Scots' Nations League B opener against Slovenia and his debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland.

A trip to face North Macedonia on 3 October follows before a home tie with Slovenia three days afterwards.

And the Belgian said: "We have a good mix between experienced players, new faces, first cap players, young lads, players who are back.

"We have a lot of leaders, we have a lot of players who know how to win games.

"We want to be ambitious in this Nations League. We have to use this Nations League to try things, to experiment things but the most important is to be ambitious."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr script history, break Argentine club's 87-year-old record
articles.summary: Football News: Cristiano Ronaldo-led Al Nassr have set a new record for the most consecutive matches with a goal in a top-flight league, scoring in their 94th straig.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo-led Al Nassr have set a new record for the most consecutive matches with a goal in a top-flight league, scoring in their 94th straight game to surpass a mark that had stood for 87 years.The Saudi Pro League record was confirmed on Saturday when substitute Abdullah Al-Hamdan scored from long range to earn Al Nassr a 1-1 draw against Al Khaleej. The goal took Al Nassr past the previous record of 93 consecutive league matches set by Buenos Aires-based Club Atlético River Plate between September 1936 and June 1939.Al Nassr's run began on December 8, 2023, when they beat Al Riyadh 4-1. Their previous league match without a goal had been a 3-0 defeat to Al Hilal. Since then, Ronaldo and his teammates have scored in every Saudi Pro League match they have played.The draw against Al Khaleej also completed Al Nassr's preparations for their AFC Champions League Elite campaign. They will begin their continental campaign away against Al Ain on September 16.Last season, Al Nassr played in the AFC Champions League Two and reached the final after winning all 10 of their matches before losing 1-0 to Gamba Osaka.Ronaldo returned to Al Nassr after Portugal's early exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup for what he has indicated will likely be his final season in professional football. The 41-year-old won the Saudi Pro League in May 2026, his first major trophy in Riyadh, and will now look to defend the title in his 25th professional season.Ronaldo missed the season opener against Al-Fateh after returning from his wedding to Georgina Rodriguez. He made his return on August 21, coming off the bench to score his 977th career goal. articles.title: Northern Ireland: Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill and Everton's Braiden Graham retain places in squad for Nations League
articles.summary: Premier League teenagers Ceadach O'Neill and Braiden Graham keep their places in Northern Ireland's squad for the upcoming Nations League quadruple-header.
articles.body:
Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill and Everton's Braiden Graham have kept their places in Northern Ireland's squad for the upcoming Nations League quadruple-header.

The teenage pair were called up for the first time by Michael O'Neill for June friendlies against Guinea and France, with the Arsenal 18-year-old appearing in both games.

Defenders Dan Ballard, Paddy McNair, Terry Devlin and Eoin Toal have all returned to the squad after missing the June games.

Also back after not featuring in the summer are goalkeepers Bailey Peacock-Farrell and Conor Hazard, as well as striker Dion Charles.

There is a place in the squad for Michael Forbes too. The Dundee United defender won his only previous cap against Finland in 2023.

Liverpool full-back Conor Bradley, who has not played since January after knee surgery, remains absent and has been joined on the sidelines by Preston North End midfielder Ali McCann and Aberdeen's Brad Lyons.

After promotion from the third tier last year, Northern Ireland start their 2026 Nations League B campaign with an away trip to Georgia on 25 September and conclude the window at home to the same opposition on 5 October.

In between they face Hungary in Belfast and Ukraine in Slovakia.

With four games in just an 11-day span, Michael O'Neill has called up 28 players after only selecting 23 for the previous window in June.

The manager also has goalkeepers Luke Southwood and Josh Clarke, along with striker Jamie Reid on standby.

Goalkeepers: Pierce Charles (Queens Park Rangers, on loan from Manchester City), Conor Hazard (Wycombe Wanderers), Bailey Peacock-Farrell (Blackpool).

Defenders: Tom Atcheson (Blackburn Rovers), Ruairi McConville (Norwich City), Trai Hume (Sunderland), Ciaron Brown (Oxford United), Brodie Spencer (Oxford United), Dan Ballard (Sunderland), Paddy McNair (Hull City), Eoin Toal (Bolton Wanderers), Terry Devlin (Portsmouth), Michael Forbes (Dundee United)

Midfielders: Jordan Thompson (Preston North End), Shea Charles (Fulham), Jamie McDonnell (Oxford United), Justin Devenny (Stoke City), Paul Smyth (Queens Park Rangers), Isaac Price (West Bromwich Albion), Patrick Kelly (Barnsley), Ethan Galbraith (Stoke City), Kieran Morrison (Sheffield Wednesday, on loan from Liverpool).

Forwards: Josh Magennis (Stevenage), Jamie Donley (Luton Town, on loan from Tottenham Hotspur), Dion Charles (Blackpool, on loan from Huddersfield Town), Callum Marshall (Luton Town), Ceadach O'Neill (Arsenal), Braiden Graham (Everton).

Live coverage of all six of Northern Ireland's 2026 Nations League games will be on BBC NI, BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app with radio coverage on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster.

articles.title: Fábio Silva ha despertado: “En el fútbol, y en la vida, las cosas no son siempre fáciles”
articles.standfirst: El ex de Las Palmas ha generado cinco goles con el Borussia Dortmund en los primeros cinco partidos del curso
articles.summary: El ex de Las Palmas ha generado cinco goles con el Borussia Dortmund en los primeros cinco partidos del curso
articles.body: La explosión de Fábio Silva (Oporto, 2002) durante su cesión en Las Palmas hace dos temporadas le valió para desvincularse, por fin, del Wolverhampton y fichar por el Borussia Dortmund a cambio de 22.5 millones de euros. Su primer curso en Alemania, tras llegar lesionado, fue bastante complicado. Pero, superado el proceso de adaptación, parece que está comenzando a despertar. “Estoy muy satisfecho con Fábio en general. Pero tenemos muchos jugadores de calidad arriba. Ahora mismo, se está quedando corto. Pero espero que en un futuro cercano veamos más apariciones suyas”, declaró en noviembre de 2025 un Niko Kovac al que no le terminó de entrar por el ojo. Prueba de ello es que acabó la temporada con apenas 10 titularidades en los 39 partidos que disputó. Le dio tiempo, eso sí, a fabricar una decena de goles. Las perspectivas, verdaderamente, no eran mucho más optimistas de cara a esta campaña. “Conoce cuál su rol en el equipo. Guirassy es nuestra primera opción en la delantera. Él es el desafiante”, llegó a apuntar Niko Kovac durante el verano. Unas palabras que mantuvieron el nombre de Fábio Silva entre los candidatos a cambiar de aires hasta el cierre del mercado. Su entorno reconoce que hubo propuesta de las cinco grandes ligas y Turquía. En MARCA, de hecho, se informó que la Real fue quien más interés pareció mostrar. “No sé qué va a pasar. Quiero ser más importante. Si digo otra cosa, estaría mintiendo”, expuso el luso. La grave lesión sufrida por Konstantelias hizo que permaneciese en el Signal Iduna Park y, cada vez que Kovac le ha ido dando minutos, ha respondido: marcó ante el Bayern en la Supercopa alemana y, tras no participar frente al Hamburgo en el estreno de la Bundesliga, volvió a ver puerta en POKAL, firmó el 2-2 ante el Hoffenheim, asistió en Champions frente al Villarreal y, en su primera titularidad en Liga, ‘abrió la lata’ contra el Paderborn. “En el fútbol, y en la vida, las cosas no son siempre fáciles. La temporada pasada y también al principio de esta campaña hubo mucho ruido a mi alrededor”, reconoció tras el choque ante el Paderborn un Fábio Silva que no sólo está demostrando poder convivir con Guirassy… sino que le está viniendo bien jugar unos metros por detrás con mayor cuota de libertad. “No soy un ‘9’ normal. Soy un ‘9.5’”, se definía a sí mismo. Es, de hecho, el segundo jugador del Borussia Dortmund que más regates con éxito (1.5) está promediando y, además, también el segundo que ha registrado una mayor punta de velocidad (35.4 km/h). "Durante las vacaciones incidió bastante en la preparación física", nos cuentan. “Cuando un jugador reacciona así, y todas las partes dan un paso hacia el otro, muestra ese impulso y ese rendimiento en el campo, resulta muy positivo para todos”, expresó Ole Book, director deportivo del Borussia Dortmund. “Lo está haciendo muy bien. Como entrenador, siempre tengo diferentes opciones en mente y una de ellas es jugar con dos delanteros”, decía Kovac. Fábio Silva quería más protagonismo y, desde luego, se lo está ganando. Parece haber ‘despertado’… y espera darle continuidad a lo largo de la temporada.

articles.title: Uefa: Cardiff's Principality Stadium to host women's Champions League final in 2029
articles.summary: Uefa have confirmed a number of host appointments for upcoming finals, with Cardiff's Principality Stadium set to host the 2029 women's Champions League final.
articles.body:
Cardiff's Principality Stadium will host the women's Champions League final in 2029.

The 73,931-seater venue hosted the men's final between Real Madrid and Juventus in 2017 and will now welcome Europe's elite female talents later this decade.

"It's brilliant news for Cymru and the FAW and the journey that we're on, particularly in the women's game," said Football Association of Wales (FAW) chief executive Noel Mooney.

It comes nine years after Cardiff City Stadium hosted the women's Champions League final between Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon - with the latter winning on penalties following a goalless draw after extra-time.

The Cardiff city centre venue will be named National Stadium of Wales for the event to comply with Uefa sponsorship rules.

Mooney added: "This is about much more than one night in 2029. Our ambition is for the Uefa women's Champions League final to become a catalyst for the continued transformation of women's and girls' football in Wales."

Earlier this year, Principality Stadium - the largest stadium in Wales, and owned by the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) - hosted the FA Community Shield as reigning Premier League champions Arsenal won 3-0 against Manchester City.

"This is a hugely significant moment for women's sport in Wales and across Europe," said WRU group chief executive Abi Tierney.

"We are absolutely delighted that our stadium has been selected to host the 2029 Uefa women's Champions League final, bringing one of the biggest occasions in world football to Cardiff and Wales.

"The rapid growth of women's sport continues to inspire new generations of athletes and supporters, and hosting an event of this magnitude at the National Stadium of Wales is a powerful statement about the importance and future of the women's game."

Uefa have also confirmed Munich will host the 2028 men's Champions League final with Barcelona staging the final a year later, 30 years on from Manchester United's dramatic triumph over Bayern Munich in the Spanish city.

The 2028 women's Champions League final will take place at Parc Olympic Lyonnais.

It has also been announced that the National Arena in Bucharest will host the 2028 Europa League final. The National Stadium in Belgrade will hold the Europa League final a year later.

Turin's iconic Juventus Stadium will host the 2028 Conference League final. The Puskas Arena in Budapest will host the 2029 showpiece.

• 2028: Parc Olympic Lyonnais, Lyon-Décines

• 2029: National Stadium of Wales, Cardiff

• 2029: National Stadium Serbia, Belgrade

articles.summary: Sufre una rotura fibrilar en el recto anterior del muslo izquierdo
articles.body: Las pruebas médicas confirmaron la lesión muscular de Iago Aspas. El capitán sufre una rotura fibrilar en el recto anterior del muslo izquierdo que lo mantendrá de baja aproximadamente un mes. Se perderá los partidos de esta semana ante Omonia de Nicosia y Racing de Santander y es duda para los encuentros ante Elche y Juventus a la vuelta del parón. La lesión se produjo en los primeros instantes que estuvo en el terreno de juego en el partido de Liga de este domingo ante el Málaga, disputado en Balaídos. Esta temporada ha intervenido en los 6 partidos de Liga, sumando 220 minutos y habiendo marcado un gol.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Rankings after Week 2
articles.summary: The headline of the weekend belonged to Texas, which engineered a preposterous comeback to beat top-ranked Ohio State.
articles.body:
The headline of the weekend belonged to Texas, which engineered a preposterous comeback to beat top-ranked Ohio State.

As a result, Arch Manning solidified his place as a key contender in the fledgling 2026 Heisman Trophy race. He overcame a quiet opening half and guided the Longhorns to an improbable win.

Instead, that honor remains in the hands of Miami quarterback Darian Mensah because of his near-perfect two-game run.

The rankings of this weekly update are subjective but consider a mix of preseason expectations—a factor that steadily diminishes in the opening month of the regular season—and on-field production to date.

Julian Sayin, QB, Ohio State : In the first half against Texas, it seemed like Sayin and star receiver Jeremiah Smith would dominate the game. Instead, a quiet second half doomed OSU in its 20-point collapse. Sayin finished with 278 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception in the 24-23 loss.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : He was amazing in the Week 2 upset of Oregon. Mestemaker threw for 317 yards, rushed for 109 and accounted for three touchdowns in a stunning win. Also, he's tossed four interceptions in two games with a loss to Tulsa on the résumé. There is plenty left to prove here.

Dante Moore, QB, Oregon : Was that an embarrassing day or a signal of bad things to come? Moore completed just 14-of-29 passes in the loss at Oklahoma State, mustering 191 yards and two scores. He sticks on the radar, but only because it's so early in the season.

KJ Duff, WR, Rutgers : I feel a need to mention Duff, who's racked up 17 catches for 333 yards and five touchdowns. Short of Rutgers assembling a jaw-dropping turnaround—and, well, no—he won't contend for the Heisman. But that's a ridiculous two-game stretch for a strong NFL draft prospect.

Kevin Jennings, QB, SMU : After throwing for 430 yards with three touchdowns and two picks in the opening win at Florida State, Jennings padded his stats nicely opposite FCS team UC Davis. He put up 337 yards and five scores through the air. Jennings and SMU head to No. 23 Louisville in Week 3.

Gunner Stockton, Georgia : Conference play begins for Stockton in Week 3 as UGA travels to Arkansas. The senior successfully padded his stats during routs of Tennessee State and Western Kentucky, hitting 28-of-32 passes with 436 yards, eight touchdowns and zero interceptions.

Josh Hoover, Indiana : Hoover, meanwhile, has a third chance to bump up those numbers—and in Week 3, that's opposite a WKU defense that Stockton just wrecked. Hoover, who didn't play in the second half of IU's shutout over Howard last weekend, has completed 19-of-27 attempts for 376 yards and eight scores.

Sam Leavitt, LSU : Five interceptions in two games? Not exactly Heisman material. Still, he's passed for 574 yards, scampered for 135 and totaled seven touchdowns with a noteworthy win over Clemson. Leavitt is entering a critical back-to-back of showdowns at Ole Miss and home to Texas A&M.

Kamario Taylor, Mississippi State : The electric dual-threat has stuffed the stat sheet in two blowout wins. He threw for 354 yards and four touchdowns while adding 59 rushing yards and a score against Louisiana-Monroe, then put up 227 passing yards and three touchdowns with 86 yards on the ground at Minnesota. Taylor leads MSU into South Carolina on Saturday.

CJ Carr, Notre Dame : Carr shredded an overmatched Rice secondary as Notre Dame cruised to a 52-0 rout. Completing 16-of-20 passes, he ended with 253 yards and four touchdowns. Michigan State is up next.

Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss : Chambliss followed a solid evening in the tight win over Louisville with an crisp showing opposite Charlotte. He went 23-of-26 with 225 yards and two scores. The bigger story is Chambliss and Ole Miss host Leavitt and LSU—coached by former Ole Miss boss Lane Kiffin—in Week 3.

Rocco Becht, Penn State : During wins against Marshall and Temple, the Iowa State transfer has connected on 34-of-45 attempts with 537 yards and seven touchdowns to zero interceptions. Becht may have another big game on the horizon as Penn State hosts Buffalo.

Thanks to USC opening its season in Week 0, Jayden Maiava has compiled the most impressive stats in the country at this point.

Altogether, he's completed 67-of-83 passes for 896 yards—a sharp 10.8-yard average per attempt—with 10 touchdowns and a lone interception. Maiava has also scored once on the ground, leading the Trojans to a 3-0 start.

That, of course, was the expectation with games against San Jose State, Fresno State and Louisiana. USC should be 4-0 after playing at Rutgers this week, too.

Beginning in Week 4, the Trojans host Oregon and Washington before traveling to Penn State. What happens during that stretch will have a significant impact on Maiava's place in the Heisman hierarchy.

Remove the emotion of Texas' wild comeback to shock Ohio State, and Arch Manning didn't have an incredible day overall.

While hitting 23-of-37 passes, he passed for 195 yards—just 5.3 per attempt—with one touchdown. The interception took a freaky carom and wasn't his fault, although he slightly overthrew a likely touchdown in the first place.

Yet when the Longhorns needed a spark, he excelled.

Beginning with a key fourth-down conversion late in the third quarter, Manning went 11-of-15 for 127 yards with a score through the end of the game. His mobility made a key difference down the stretch, too.

Propelling a 20-point surge to beat the nation's top-ranked team is a heck of a bullet point on a Heisman résumé.

Following his record-setting performance in the opening demolition of Stanford, Malachi Toney had another solid day.

Toney reeled in four passes for 96 yards and a touchdown as Miami steamrolled lower-division Florida A&M 77-7. He added a 22-yard punt return, then stayed on the sideline for the whole second half.

Given that Purdue just threw for 329 yards against Wake's secondary, Toney may have another explosive performance in store on Friday night.

Toney enters the contest with 16 receptions for 330 yards and four scores.

The result didn't go Ohio State's way. Jeremiah Smith, nevertheless, was clearly the most talented player on the field.

Smith nabbed three passes on the Buckeyes' first touchdown drive, snared a 43-yard reception to set up a field goal and punctuated a dominant opening half with a 19-yard touchdown. He ended with eight catches for 164 yards and that score.

However, the danger zone in Heisman Trophy voting historically is around three losses. I'll reassess if OSU crumbles, but that's not a factor today.

Smith, who's posted 16 receptions for 315 yards and three touchdowns, narrowly edges out Toney due to peak competition level.

Darian Mensah completed 27-of-30 passes for 401 yards and five touchdowns during the Week 1 demolition of Stanford. Then, against FAMU, he went 14-of-15 with 252 yards and three scores.

So far, Mensah leads the nation with a 91.1 completion rate, is second at 14.5 yards per attempt and tied for third with eight touchdown passes.

You could literally ask for more, but—practically speaking—he's been flawless.

While road games must always be respected, Friday's trip to Wake Forest looks favorable on paper for Mensah, Toney and the 'Canes.

articles.title: Scotland: Robbie Ure, Luis Binks and Colby Donovan among five newcomers included in Sebastien Pocognoli's first squad
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli has handed first full call-ups to five new players; Scotland play Slovenia away on September 26 in their first match under the new head coach, followed by three more Nations League games against Switzerland at home, North Macedonia away and Slovenia at Hampden
articles.body:
Celtic defender Colby Donovan , Hearts winger Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh of Swansea City are also included for the upcoming Nations League games.

There is also a long-awaited recall for Hull City striker Oli McBurnie who won his last international cap in 2021.

Goalkeepers Scott Bain and Jon McCracken are back in following Craig Gordon's decision to retire after the World Cup.

Napoli's Billy Gilmour returns after a knee injury forced him to withdraw from former boss Steve Clarke's final squad.

Luke Graham is included after being part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May, following a breakthrough season with Dundee.

The Stoke City defender, who has been capped three times at under-21 level, has played every minute as The Potters picked up three wins and a draw in their last four Championship games.

Josh Doig and Kieron Bowie of Serie A club Sassuolo, Lennon Miller of Udinese and Hearts forward James Wilson have also been recalled.

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay is missing as he recovers from minor heart surgery. Rangers striker Lawrence Shankland is sidelined with a hamstring issue, with Torino's Che Adams also injured.

A total of 12 players who went to the World Cup are missing from the Belgian's first squad.

Rangers' John Souttar , Anthony Ralston of Celtic, Hibernian defender Grant Hanley , Wrexham's Dominic Hyam , Tyler Fletcher of Manchester United, Millwall's Lyndon Dkyes , Stoke forward George Hirst and Swansea's Ross Stewart are also not included.

Defender Binks is the captain of Danish SuperLiga side Brondby.

The 25-year-old has previously represented Scotland at U18 level before playing for England youth.

Former Rangers academy product Ure secured a mega-move to LaLiga club Sevilla after an impressive spell at Swedish side Sirius where he netted 20 goals in 20 matches.

The 22-year-old is also eligible to play for Ukraine through the grandparent rule.

McPake has been rewarded for his impressive form since his summer switch to Hearts from St Johnstone, while Swansea's Welsh comes in after his successful loan spell at Motherwell from Celtic last season.

Right-back Donovan has featured in all of Celtic's games so far this season and replaces his Hoops team-mate Ralston.

Goalkeepers: Scott Bain (Falkirk), Angus Gunn (San Jose Earthquakes), Liam Kelly (Rangers), Jon McCracken (Bradford City)

Defenders: Luis Binks (Brondby), Josh Doig (Sassuolo), Colby Donovan (Celtic), Luke Graham (Stoke City), Jack Hendry (Al-Ettifaq), Aaron Hickey (Brentford), Scott McKenna (Dinamo Zagreb), Nathan Patterson (Torino), Andy Robertson (Tottenham), Kieran Tierney (Celtic), Stephen Welsh (Swansea City)

Midfielders: Ryan Christie (Bournemouth), Lewis Ferguson (Bologna), Billy Gilmour (Napoli), John McGinn (Aston Villa), Kenny McLean (Norwich City), Josh McPake (Hearts), Lennon Miller (Udinese)

Forwards: Kieron Bowie (Sassuolo), Findlay Curtis (Rangers), Ben Gannon-Doak (Bournemouth), Oli McBurnie (Hull City), Robbie Ure (Sevilla), James Wilson (Hearts)

Former Scotland striker James McFadden on Sky Sports News:

"Robbie Ure is one that has been on the radar for his form in Sweden in particular, towards the run-up to the World Cup, but missed out on the squad.

"Getting that move to Sevilla shows that he has the capabilities to go and play at the highest level.

"It's an area that we've struggled with for a number of years and for Scotland to bring competition.

"Robbie Ure's taken an unconventional route. He definitely deserves a respect because he's been brave to move away and forge a career elsewhere and probably be allowed to develop and focus on himself to get to this point."

On McBurnie's recall, McFadden added: "Oli deserves his opportunity and there's been a bit of a backlash towards Oli over the last few years.

"I know how passionate he is about playing for Scotland. He's had to be patient but again another one that's gone away and worked on himself and focused on himself.

"Got back to the Premier League and Oli is definitely worth coming in and having a look at to see if he can go and make that number nine spot his own."

Slovenia vs Scotland - September 26, kick-off 2pm

Scotland vs Switzerland - September 29, kick-off 7.45pm

articles.title: Report Card Grades for College Football's Top QBs after Week 2
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's production through the air and on the ground, their game outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 14-of-16, 337 yards, 5 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 5 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (UC Davis) Week 2 Outcome: Win (56-10)

After a shaky Week 1 performance against Florida State, where he threw two interceptions and struggled to find a rhythm early, Kevin Jennings was nearly perfect against an overmatched UC Davis squad on Saturday.

With eight touchdown passes already this year, he now sits just 10 away from passing Tanner Mordecai to become SMU's all-time leader. The more immediate focus will be surviving a tough Week 3 matchup on the road against a good Louisville team.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 18-of-29, 212 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 13 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (UCF) Week 2 Outcome: Win (12-7)

Mason Heintschel earned a spot in our Week 2 article with an absurd 453-yard, seven-touchdown game against Miami (OH) in Pitt's opener. While he had a much quieter follow-up performance, Pitt still won against a quality opponent.

After throwing for 2,354 yards and 16 touchdowns as a true freshman in 2025, Heintschel has some legitimate upside. There is a good chance this won't be his only appearance in our top 20 rankings over the course of the 2026 season.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 19-of-29, 292 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 2 carries, 8 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Kansas) Week 2 Outcome: Win (38-21)

After losing his starting job to Trinidad Chambliss at Ole Miss last season, Austin Simmons has landed on his feet nicely at Missouri, and through two games, he has 544 passing yards and seven touchdowns.

His 218.3 passer rating currently trails only Gunner Stockton (284.5) among SEC quarterbacks, which notably puts him ahead of the aforementioned Chambliss (170.4), who sits sixth on the list. It's still early days, but the change of scenery looks like a great fit.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 21-of-27, 268 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 11 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Temple) Week 2 Outcome: Win (27-9)

After starting the game with a missed field goal, punt, turnover on downs and a 10-play drive that ended in a field goal, the Penn State offense finally came to life late in the second quarter.

Rocco Becht had another strong individual performance piloting a familiar offense in an unfamiliar uniform in his second game after following head coach Matt Campbell from Iowa State to Penn State. Chalk up the slow start on Saturday to a unique environment, as it was a neutral-site game at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 9-of-12, 120 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, 6 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Southern) Week 2 Outcome: Win (77-6)

Houston found the end zone in each of their 11 offensive possessions before their final drive brought the 77-6 blowout to a merciful end. Conner Weigman was only under center for the first five drives of the onslaught.

The dynamic dual-threat ability that saw him rack up 2,705 passing yards, 700 rushing yards and 36 total touchdowns a year ago will need to be firing on all cylinders next weekend when they head to Lubbock to take on No. 13 Texas Tech.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 26-of-41, 249 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, 56 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Utah State) Week 2 Outcome: Win (16-14)

Despite a 2-0 start, Washington tumbled out of the AP Top 25 this week following a narrow escape against a Utah State team that checked in at No. 137 on The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams heading into Week 2.

It was also a second straight lackluster showing from Demond Williams Jr., coming off an inconsistent performance in the Apple Cup in Week 1. He will look to turn the tide against FCS opponent Eastern Washington on Saturday.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 15-of-25, 163 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 17 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Arizona State) Week 2 Outcome: Win (48-20)

It took 24 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, including a pair of defensive touchdowns, for Texas A&M to pull away from Arizona State in a game that was much closer than the final score suggests.

Marcel Reed is averaging just 7.2 yards per attempt through two games this season, down from 8.4 a year ago. This is despite the dynamic one-two punch of Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton at wide receiver.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 23-of-31, 230 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, 38 yards, 1 TD Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (BYU) Week 2 Outcome: Loss (17-28)

Noah Fifita is now 0-3 in his career against BYU following Saturday's loss. The Arizona offense could only muster three punts and a turnover on downs in the second half after taking a 17-14 lead into halftime.

Fifita's first-quarter interception also came at Arizona's own 23-yard line and gave the Cougars terrific field position that was cashed in two plays later for their first touchdown of the game.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 17-of-33, 189 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, 45 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Michigan) Week 2 Outcome: Loss (10-17)

After cruising against UTEP in Week 1, John Mateer failed to come up with the big play when Oklahoma needed it in a Week 2 loss to Michigan that sent them tumbling down the AP Top 25.

An Oklahoma field goal early in the fourth quarter made it a 10-10 game. The defense forced an immediate three-and-out, but Mateer handed the momentum right back with a crucial interception. The Wolverines capitalized with the go-ahead touchdown. Oklahoma managed just 25 total yards across 13 plays in their final three offensive possessions.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 6-of-11, 145 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 18 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Howard) Week 2 Outcome: Win (55-0)

Josh Hoover needed just 11 pass attempts to record his second straight four-touchdown game. Three of those went to Charlie Becker, who has now hauled in five of Hoover's eight touchdown passes this year.

He also surpassed 10,000 career passing yards on Saturday, becoming the 166th quarterback in college football history to eclipse that mark. His 10,005 passing yards lead all active passers, ahead of Rocco Becht (9,813) and Noah Fifita (9,692).

Week 2 Passing Stats: 13-of-16, 234 yards, 5 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, 3 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Western Kentucky) Week 2 Outcome: Win (70-20)

Through two abridged games this season, Gunner Stockton has more touchdown passes (8) than incompletions (4), as he has completed 28 of 32 pass attempts for 436 yards in blowout wins against Tennessee State and Western Kentucky.

There is not much to be learned from those performances, aside from the simple fact that Georgia was the far superior team, but things ramp up quickly in the coming weeks as SEC play gets underway. The Bulldogs face Arkansas on the road this weekend, followed by a home game against a tough Oklahoma defense.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 18-of-24, 261 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, 50 yards, 2 TD Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Arkansas) Week 2 Outcome: Win (43-10)

Devon Dampier's dual-threat skills were on full display in a convincing Saturday night win against Arkansas, as he logged 311 total yards and four touchdowns, continuing to make it clear that the nagging injuries that hampered him a year ago are in the rearview.

His lone interception came on an underthrown pass. He was hit right as he released the ball, so it was more about pressure than poor decision-making. Dampier also responded with four straight touchdown drives following the turnover, effectively putting the game out of reach.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 16-of-20, 253 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: N/A Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Rice) Week 2 Outcome: Win (52-0)

As he continues to take on a more prominent role in the offense this season, CJ Carr drew the praise of head coach Marcus Freeman after dismantling the Rice defense in a nearly flawless performance.

"His decisions are impeccable," Freeman told reporters . "Last week he made the right decision 99% of the time. This week it felt like he was making the right decision, and getting us in the right protections, the right checks, all those different things that he does."

Week 2 Passing Stats: 23-of-37, 195 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 24 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Ohio State) Week 2 Outcome: Win (24-23)

The raw numbers might not jump off the page, but consider where we were a year ago, following the Ohio State vs. Texas matchup.

Arch Manning finished 17-of-30 passing for 170 yards with a touchdown and an interception in that game. The Longhorns took a 14-7 loss in the season opener as part of a disappointing 3-2 start to the year.

A touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo early in the fourth quarter kicked off a stunning comeback from down 23-3. Manning orchestrated a 12-play, 73-yard drive in under four minutes to set up the game-winning touchdown run by Hollywood Smothers.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 25-of-38, 344 yards, 1 TD, 3 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, 22 yards, 3 TD Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Louisiana Tech) Week 2 Outcome: Win (45-14)

On the one hand, 366 total yards of offense and four touchdowns are a significant level of contribution that led to LSU ultimately walking away with a comfortable 45-14 victory.

However, it's difficult to ignore those three interceptions against what was perceived to be a far inferior opponent, given the staggering 35.5-point spread. All three certainly looked like Leavitt's fault, as two came in the end zone and one led to a 100-yard return for a touchdown. Those mistakes won't be as easy to sweep under the rug once SEC play is in full swing.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 14-of-29, 191 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, -9 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Oklahoma State) Week 2 Outcome: Loss (31-39)

Facing an Oklahoma State team that lost to Tulsa in Week 1, the Ducks offense went punt, punt, turnover on downs, punt and punt to begin the game, digging a 17-7 hole in the process.

After finding some rhythm after the slow start, Dante Moore hit a wall again in clutch time, as he had two possessions to try to flip a one-possession game and the offense logged negative four yards across seven plays. The final stat line doesn't look as disastrous for Moore's overall performance. Oregon's College Football Playoff hopes took a major blow after the result.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 23-of-26, 225 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 2 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Charlotte) Week 2 Outcome: Win (41-9)

Considering he played into the fourth quarter against a Charlotte team that was No. 138 in The Athletic's 1-138 rankings, Trinidad Chambliss ideally would have put up a gaudier individual stat line.

That said, the result here was never in doubt as Ole Miss built a 27-0 halftime lead before switching to cruise control. It's hard to argue with a 23-of-26 passing performance even if it didn't lead to dizzying yardage or touchdown totals.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 19-of-29, 261 yards, 5 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: N/A Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Louisiana) Week 2 Outcome: Win (49-30)

The overall numbers are a bit deceiving right now, since Jayden Maiava and USC have played one more game than most teams because of their Week 0 matchup, but the stat line is staggering nonetheless.

Through three games: 67-of-83, 896 yards, 10 TD, 1 INT

His interception came on the first drive of the game after the pocket collapsed. It was an ill-advised throw, but he responded with touchdown passes on each of the Trojans' next three drives.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 17-of-32, 278 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, -7 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Texas) Week 2 Outcome: Loss (23-24)

After leading the nation by completing 77 percent of his passes a year ago, then connecting on 21-of-25 attempts in the season opener against Ball State, a certain level of efficiency has become Julian Sayin's calling card.

His 53.1 percent completion rate on Saturday was the worst single-game showing of his career as a starter. While his interception was a non-factor coming on a last-second heave at the end of regulation, a pair of three-and-outs and a stalled drive that ended in a missed field goal down the stretch opened the door for the Texas comeback.

Week 2 Passing Stats: 14-of-15, 252 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 2 Rushing Stats: 2 carries, 21 yards Week 2 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Florida A&M) Week 2 Outcome: Win (77-7)

Darian Mensah only played the first half of Friday night's lopsided win against Florida A&M, but that was more than enough for him to add some nice padding to his early Heisman resume.

Malachi Toney (4 catches, 96 yards, 1 TD) again served as his go-to target while padding his own award case. The Miami offense went on to pile up a school-record 856 total yards in a blowout win. A road game against Wake Forest next weekend will provide the Hurricanes' first real test.

To keep things fresh and include breakout performers, we will re-rank the top 20 quarterbacks each week on this final slide. That will then reset the field for next week's report cards.

With only two games in the books for most of these players, preseason expectations still serve as the backbone of these rankings, though a few new names joined the mix while others fell out due to a lackluster start to the new season.

1. Darian Mensah, Miami 2. Jayden Maiava, USC 3. Arch Manning, Texas 4. Devon Dampier, Utah 5. Gunner Stockton, Georgia 6. Josh Hoover, Indiana 7. CJ Carr, Notre Dame 8. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss 9. Julian Sayin, Ohio State 10. Kamario Taylor, Mississippi State 11. Austin Simmons, Missouri 12. Rocco Becht, Penn State 13. Lincoln Kienholz, Louisville 14. Kevin Jennings, SMU 15. Conner Weigman, Houston 16. Marcel Reed, Texas A&M 17. Dante Moore, Oregon 18. Sam Leavitt, LSU 19. Bear Bachmeier, BYU 20. Anthony Colandrea, Nebraska

articles.title: Luis García Plaza, sobre el Dépor: "Está invicto porque está haciendo las cosas muy bien"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Sevilla se deshizo en halagos hacia Antonio Hidalgo en el Deportivo
articles.summary: El técnico del Sevilla se deshizo en halagos hacia Antonio Hidalgo en el Deportivo
articles.body: Este martes, Luis García Plaza compareció en la previa de la quinta jornada de LaLiga EA Sports, en la que el Sevilla visitará Riazor para medirse al Deportivo de La Coruña. "El equipo está muy ilusionado, con muchas ganas. Cuando estás en positivo se nota la alegría y la confianza, pero cada partido es una historia", explicó el entrenador nervionense. Deportivo. "Está invicto porque está haciendo las cosas muy bien. Hay que analizar su trayectoria, con un músculo económico que no tiene nada que ver con un recién ascendido. A partir de ahí, la dirección deportiva ha hecho un trabajo buenísimo, ha firmado muy buenos jugadores, con mucha experiencia y apostando también por jugadores con futuro. Luego, el míster ha hecho un trabajo excepcional. Le doy mucho valor porque sé lo difícil que es ascender. Su estrella el otro día en el minuto 90 se pega un sprint para defender un contraataque del Getafe, por poner un ejemplo. Es un equipo con muchos registros". Cardoso. "Cuando pasa un tiempo y ya ha terminado el mercado, lo normal es que entrene con nosotros. Sabe su situación y que tiene que encontrar una salida. Pero es jugador del Sevilla a todos los efectos y entrena como uno más. Es un chaval excepcional. A veces, cuando tomas una decisión deportiva te duele a nivel personal porque el año pasado se comportó bien conmigo". Presión alta. "Es un poco mi idea de juego siempre, ir a buscar los partidos y estar en campo contrario. Hay veces que no lo consigues y conlleva sus riesgos. En ese aspecto si somos de los mejores es porque es el carácter del equipo e intentamos en casa estar la mayor parte del partido en campo contrario". Rotar en Riazor. "No hay problema, no hay que hacer rotaciones obligadas, después del miércoles veremos y si después del miércoles si me dicen que hay riesgo de lesión no va a jugar y si el equipo está bien repetiremos mucha gente. Si hay un pequeño riesgo, fuera". Plan de partido. "Antonio tiene muy bien trabajado al equipo en su estilo. Lo más importante es que saben a lo que juegan, con defectos y virtudes. El otro día vi que corrigen mucho según va el partido y si ven que no va como esperan varían un poco, en ataque y en defensa, son un poco como nosotros, tiene muchos registros y el trabajo del míster es muy bueno. Lo han hecho muy bien todos en verano". Marcao. "Le queda tiempo, hasta que no pase el parón, otra cosa es que no quede otra, pero necesita dos o tres semanas más de entrenamiento para participar. Necesita entrenar más". Mejora de los delanteros. "Cuando hablo de lucidez es de inspiración, a veces la acción sale bien o mal, no es falta de calidad, incluso Messi, que ha fallado penaltis. El partido fue muy completo, igual jugamos peor en Riazor pero los de arriba están más inspirados y ganamos". Nico Guillén: "La entrada de Fofana ha restado minutos y entre los damnificados es Nico, será Guridi, Kocho e incluso Lucien. Nico es joven, si alguien ha demostrado que no tiene miedo a ponerlo soy yo, tiene que hacer lo del otro día, que hizo un partidazo e hizo una segunda parte brutal. No sólo Nico, pero si alabamos el fichaje de Fofana no podemos echar tanto de menos a Nico, nos contradecimos. Eso hace que todos pierdan minutos". Solidez defensiva. "Cada uno tenemos nuestras armas, pero tenemos que encajar y recibir lo mínimo. Luego analizamos los goles que te meten y estamos bien colocados". Rubén Vargas. "Creemos, no te puedo decir, pero lo que nos llega es que va bien y que el parón de tres semanas hará una mini pretemporada y puede estar, ojalá sea así, para la vuelta del parón disponible. Creo, no tengo aún confirmación". Posibles penaltis con el Valencia. "Lo que tenemos que hacer es que en una liga larga hay decisiones que te favorecen y te quitan. No digo que no llevasen razón en BIlbao, pero la que se montó por una jugada puntual... Nos hemos quedado dos veces con diez y uno lo ganamos y otro puntuamos. Hay aciertos y errores en las acciones. Podría haber pitado penalti, sobre todo en la segunda de Castrín, pero hay que respetarlo". Sevillismo en Riazor. "La gente está ilusionada y estamos muy felices que estén así, agradecer a toda la gente que va a ir, no les puedo prometer que ganemos o empatemos, pero sí que nos vamos a dejar la vida. La afición del Sevilla sabe cuándo su equipo está dando el máximo. Esto nos motiva más a seguir con la línea de trabajo". Félix Correia. "Los jugadores necesitan adaptación, como todos. El más acertado de arriba en el trabajo fue Isaac, pero él estuvo al nivel de los demás, no muy acertado al inicio, pero me gustó cómo se rehízo y contento con todos".

articles.title: Luís Castro: "A pesar de plantar cara al Barça, no existe ninguna euforia"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués ha admitido que le sorprendió la reacción de la gente tras el tanto de Adeyemi
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués ha admitido que le sorprendió la reacción de la gente tras el tanto de Adeyemi
articles.body: "No lo había visto en mi vida". De esta manera ha afirmado Luís Castro, tras vivir en primera persona la reacción de la afición del Levante tras el tanto recibido por parte de Adeyemi en el descanso del choque del pasado domingo. Así mismo, ha admitido que no existe ningún estado de euforia tras el choque ante el cuadro culé y que, a pesar del escaso tiempo entre ambos partidos, el equipo está preparado para enfrentarse ante el Athletic Club. Recuperación tras el Barça "Está claro que si tuviéramos más días de recuperación, prepararíamos el partido con más identidad. Los jugadores van a estar preparados para el partido y, aunque sea poco tiempo, tenemos que estar porque esto es la competición. Tienes que adaptarte" Hugo Sotelo "El club ya ha hecho un comunicado. Estamos pendientes de su evolución" Athletic Club "El primer partido no fue tan bueno como es habitualmente, pero ahora ya está en una dinámica muy fuerte. Estos últimos tres han sido muy buenos y es un club que conocemos muy bien. Tienen mucha calidad individual y colectivamente no ha cambiado mucho. Esto les da estabilidad. Tiene pequeños cambios pero no tantos. Sabemos el nivel y es uno de los mejores equipos del campeonato" Axel Tape "Depende. También es el que ha venido más tarde. Necesita su tiempo para adaptarse, pero no miramos por esto. Jugarán los que están mejor para este partido. Antes del partido pensamos en algunos cambios, por si quieres jugar de una forma o de otra. Lo veremos si tiene que debutar o no" Falta de acierto en la última decisión ante el Barça "Es un partido que ya pasó. Pero, si piensas en el partido, tuvimos más oportunidades y remates que el Barça. Hasta ahora no había ocurrido esto. Yo pienso que los jugadores hicieron un buen partido y el nivel colectivo estuvo muy bien. Ellos hicieron el partido que estuvieron más acertados, ya que todas las que tuvieron las marcaron. Ahora toca mirando adelante" Gestión emocional "Yo pienso que a mi nadie me mira con euforia. Ellos lo saben. No hay euforia. Después del partido de Barça yo no estaba contento y ellos, tampoco. Eso es bueno. No están contento con el partido y sabemos que la liga es muy dura y no será fácil para ningún equipo. No existe tal euforia" Margen de mejora "Siempre hay mucha. Cuando estás ganando, también hay margen de mejora. Para el momento de temporada y con los cambios que salieron, estamos a buen nivel. Las contrataciones han sido buenas y han aportado. Esto nos ayudan a estar más cerca. Para le tiempo que estamos trabajanado, estamos a un buen nivel. articles.title: As Ballon d'Or vote nears, stars campaign for the award
articles.summary: With less than two weeks to go before Ballon d'Or voting closes, many leading candidates are campaigning hard to be awarded football's top individual honour....
articles.body:
With less than two weeks to go before Ballon d'Or voting closes, many leading candidates are campaigning hard to be awarded football's top individual honour.

This self-promotion is a relatively recent development in a team sport where, until a few years ago, the top individual prize went largely unnoticed until it was time to present it.

But now, the Ballon d'Or dominates the football conversation during the months when the new European season is still finding its feet.

The trophy will be presented on October 26, while the final sprint began on September 8 when France Football, the award organiser, released the list of 30 candidates to succeed Ousmane Dembele .

The ceremony will be in London, even though only five of the 30 nominees play in the English Premier League.

The award carries no cash prize, but it has become worth increased income and status to players and their teams.

Many stars have related bonuses in their boot contracts while the award also increases their overall marketing value, and that of their club.

The two all-time leading Ballon d'Or winners, Lionel Messi , who has picked up the trophy eight times, and Cristiano Ronaldo , who won five times, both have annual sponsorship income estimated by Forbes at more than 65 million dollars.

Clubs can expect to sell more merchandise if one of their players wins.

Some 100 invited journalists –- one representative from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings -– will cast votes.

With no clear favourite, the stars and their PR agencies are stepping up their campaigns. Achievements are shamelessly paraded to scrape together votes.

"For me, Mbappe and I, we're the two best players in the world," Lamine Yamal , who has won the World Cup and La Liga in 2026, said in an interview on Movistar Plus.

"I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I deserve it because of what I've won," the 19-year-old aded.

He was responding to the Frenchman, who days earlier had emphasised the award's individual nature -- after a year in which he won no trophies with either Real Madrid or France, who lost a World Cup semi-final to Spain, but scored 10 World Cup goals to take his tally to an all-time leading 22.

"Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out, a global event. Who am I voting for? Myself," said the striker, who was also the top scorer in last season's Liga and Champions League.

His manager, Jose Mourinho, did not hesitate to back up the argument: "We know who has made history this summer, and he's not from PSG or the Spanish national team."

In 2024, Real Madrid boycotted the ceremony after learning just before they were due to travel that none of their seven nominees had won.

This year, Paris Saint-Germain have a record 10 nominees, after retaining the Champions League.

That number, and also the side's reputation for collective team spirit, may count against them.

Their leading candidates are Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Fabian Ruiz, the only player on the list to have won both the Champions League and the World Cup this year.

"Why not dream?", the unassuming Spanish midfielder told French television.

PSG are refusing to pick one individual while arguing that the winner has to be one of their players.

"Kvara and Doue are incredible players. For me Kvara could win the Ballon d'Or, as could Dembele and others," said coach Luis Enrique.

Dembele told France Football that he would not try to influence the poll.

"May the best player win; in any case, it's not us who are voting," he said. "I never sell myself. It's up to them to decide."

Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane , who scored 73 goals while leading Bayern Munich to a German domestic double and his country to third in the World Cup, remains quiet.

Bayern are speaking up for their leader, putting together a video in which team-mates said that Kane should win.

"He deserves to win it, 100 per cent, without a doubt," said Colombian Luis Diaz, who is also on the shortlist.

articles.title: Iñaki da un paso al frente y convence a De la Barrera
articles.standfirst: El extremeño suma dos partidos como titular con Las Palmas
articles.summary: El extremeño suma dos partidos como titular con Las Palmas
articles.body: Iñaki González ha dejado de llamar a la puerta. El centrocampista extremeño ha dado un paso al frente y ya suma dos titularidades consecutivas, una de ellas con Kirian viendo el inicio del partido desde el banquillo. Su irrupción está modificando el equilibrio de la medular amarilla, donde Rubén de la Barrera buscaba una pieza capaz de aportar algo más que buen trato de balón. Iñaki ha aparecido para aportar piernas, intensidad y capacidad para sostener al equipo, convirtiéndose en un futbolista cada vez más importante en los planes del técnico. Ante el Cádiz, además, volvió a formar de inicio y completó 85 minutos en el triunfo amarillo. Con Kirian y Loiodice -futbolistas de indudable calidad con la pelota- la UD había echado en falta mayor despliegue, capacidad de recuperación y presencia para proteger al equipo cuando pierde la posesión. Iñaki ofrece precisamente ese perfil. Ordena, llega, compite y, sobre todo, permite que el centro del campo tenga un futbolista pendiente de equilibrar al resto. Rubén de la Barrera no ha escondido su satisfacción con la evolución del extremeño: "Estoy especialmente contento por Iñaki porque tiene deseo, voluntad, piernas y está agregando a todo eso comprensión y conocimiento de lo que pasa. Es importante por la posición en la que juega y lo que queremos para esa posición. Lo está asumiendo y lo veo con jerarquía y peso. Al equipo le da consistencia y seguridad". Un respaldo que refleja el cambio de estatus de un futbolista que ha pasado de buscar minutos a reclamar un sitio en el once.

articles.title: Can Everton Afford to Sacrifice Cup Competitions?
articles.summary: Everton fans don't need reminding of the last time they saw their side lift silverware, and Wolves are the next opponent to stand in their way of a potential...
articles.body:
A little under a year since that bitter cup defeat at Molineux, it's déjà vu for Everton in the Carabao Cup third round as we once again face Wolverhampton Wanderers . This time, however, it's under the lights of Hill Dickinson Stadium as Everton hope to inflict revenge on the Black Country outfit.

A paper-thin Everton squad following deadline day prompted a few rumblings amongst the fanbase about not taking the cup competitions seriously. The Carabao Cup is one of those, especially considering all the rounds fall before the January window opens.

But can Everton seriously afford to sacrifice the cup competitions this season?

Even before the end of the transfer window in the build-up to Everton's second-round clash against Preston North End at Deepdale, David Moyes' comments may have foreshadowed Everton having to make a decision between league or cup this season.

Speaking to Joe Thomas at the Liverpool Echo, this is what Moyes had to say: "Of course we all want to win the cups. Yes the cups are hugely important, would it be more important than staying in the Premier League? I'll ask you the question: Is winning a cup more important than staying in the Premier League? What would your answer be?"

This prompted its fair share of debate online.

Now the transfer window is shut, the argument for sacrificing the cups is pretty straightforward. Everton have an exceptionally small squad, and after last season's late drop-off, there's an argument to suggest that protecting players for a league push should be a priority for David Moyes. Players like Jarrad Branthwaite , James Garner and Thierno Barry probably fall into this category.

It's an argument I can certainly understand. The lack of depth means that Wednesday night's game represents another hurdle to manoeuvre, praying not to see any key players pull up with an injury.

So, if the Wolves game presents an opportunity to choose between a first-team side and heavy rotation as Moyes did this time last year, there are probably more grounds to accept that decision this time around.

But there's another question worth asking. What exactly is the point of Everton saving themselves for the league?

The positive start to the season by Everton, remaining unbeaten across all competitions, has certainly eased the pressure a little bit. We look competitive in every game we play in, and the mentality is certainly dragging us over the line in games.

For me, that now means a cup run almost feels like a perfect opportunity to build momentum and really create a sense of harmony amongst the squad and fanbase. It feels like something Everton, as an entire club, needs to really galvanise everyone.

We've been starved of success in cup competitions, not winning one since Paul Rideout's goal in 1995 secured our last FA Cup. That's an entire generation of Evertonians who've never seen success, me included!

I'm not saying Moyes should start exactly how he did against Tottenham , but Everton certainly have some quality to bring into the side: Jake O'Brien, Tyler Dibling, even Jack Grealish to make his full debut on his return . For me, last year's trip to Molineux felt way more than rotation by Moyes. It felt like a decision to not take the cup seriously, and if we got through, we got through. Personally, I think those days are gone. At some stage, progress has to be measured by more than simply where we finish in the league each year.

Cup competitions nowadays represent the perfect opportunity to kick on as a football club, securing European football through winning silverware and attracting better talent in the process. A club like Crystal Palace is a prime example.

This is why, ultimately, I feel Everton cannot afford to rest ten or eleven players this time around. This feels like a massive opportunity to really put some momentum together, and even with a paper-thin squad, show a defiant squad mentality.

No doubt about it, this week is huge. An okay start could turn into a fantastic one with two wins under our belt going into the international break. Let's hope we can string a couple of results together.

What would you do? Would you focus on the league over the cup because of our squad? Let me know your thoughts!

articles.title: Flick has a chat with Barcelona midfielder struggling for minutes ahead of Racing clash
articles.summary: FC Barcelona completed their final training session on Tuesday ahead of their meeting with Racing Santander at the Spotify Camp Nou on Wednesday night.Follow...
articles.body:
FC Barcelona completed their final training session on Tuesday ahead of their meeting with Racing Santander at the Spotify Camp Nou on Wednesday night.

Following Monday's recovery session, Hansi Flick had all available players at his disposal as his side prepared for their fifth La Liga match of the season.

Before the session began, the German coach briefly spoke with Gavi at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper , as reported by Mundo Deportivo .

The midfielder has seen limited action during the opening weeks of the campaign. He started against Elche , but Flick replaced him as a precaution after he took a knock to his knee.

The injury proved to be nothing serious, but Gavi was left out of the squads for the matches against Athletic Club and Rayo Vallecano , before remaining on the bench for the 5-0 victory at Mestalla.

Gavi's prominence has taken a hit. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

He then played 11 minutes against Feyenoord in the Champions League but was an unused substitute once again in the subsequent match against Levante .

As things stand, the likes of Pedri , Rodri , and even Marc Bernal are ahead of Gavi in the pecking order, leading to him struggling for minutes in recent matches.

Wednesday's meeting with Racing could therefore provide another opportunity for Flick to manage his midfield options and give Gavi further minutes.

Flick was able to work with his entire available squad, with only Frenkie de Jong and Roony Bardghji remaining sidelined through injury.

Jesse Bisiwu also completed the session with the first team. The youngster has regularly trained alongside Flick's squad but is yet to make his senior debut for Barcelona .

Jesse Bisiwu trained with the first team. (Picture credit: x/@FCBarcelona)

Bisiwu has instead made two appearances for Barça Atletic, including a promising performance against Logrones B last weekend.

Barcelona have two matches remaining before the upcoming international break, which will be longer than usual.

After Wednesday's meeting with Racing, they will travel to Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan to face Sevilla on Saturday.

The Catalan side are looking to finish this opening stretch of the season by maintaining their advantage at the top of the table.

articles.title: INEOS have Italian serial winner at top of wishlist if they sack Michael Carrick
articles.summary: 2 One win in four league games is surely not the start to the 2026-27 Premier League campaign that Manchester United fans had hoped for.The 20-time English c...
articles.body:
One win in four league games is surely not the start to the 2026-27 Premier League campaign that Manchester United fans had hoped for.

The 20-time English champions enjoyed a run of 12 wins, three draws, and two losses in the second half of the 2025-26 Premier League season under Michael Carrick , so expectations were naturally high heading into the new campaign.

This season, however, has proven to be a frustrating ride so far.

Carrick has been handed a stronger squad than the one he inherited last term, yet he has struggled to get his side firing on all cylinders.

Doubts are consequently creeping in over his tactics and in-game decisions.

While reports suggest Old Trafford's decision-makers still believe in Carrick's project, he risks finding himself in a far trickier position if results do not improve soon.

Indeed, sources in Italy are already suggesting the Red Devils could shake up their technical bench, with a clear favourite already lined up to replace Carrick.

Corriere della Sera, via Sport Witness , report:

"Manchester United aren't entirely sure about Carrick. They are beginning to evaluate his future at the club and another managerial change could be considered soon."

Crucially, they go on to drop a bombshell, revealing that "as things stand, Conte is at the top of the Red Devils' shortlist."

Given United's desire to return to the top and restore glory to M16, the links to Conte are easy to understand.

He is a serial winner, renowned for his intense discipline, tactical brilliance, and a proven track record of transforming struggling teams into champions.

The Italian could prove to be the perfect appointment if INEOS crave instant glory, though that approach can prove unsustainable over time.

A longer-term project, as Mikel Arteta has shown at Arsenal , tends to be more sustainable, so Carrick will need to turn things around quickly enough that no shortcuts become necessary.
